steps.message:
Item 054 on the verification register for Birchwood Village Expansion, Package A has to close before 07/20/2026. It covers the slab-on-grade fill compaction testing Vantree ran on 07/08/2026 and their Field Density Report SF-26-0708, issued the next day.

Work those results against Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, and give me an acceptance determination. State the acceptance basis you are using, the limits it produces, and what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.

Cover the testing as well as the results. I want to know whether what was done and recorded is enough to support the determination under that section, and what has to be in hand before anything is built on this fill.

Two files are attached: Fill_Placement_Records_BlockA_SlabOnGrade.xlsx, the Contractor's placement log for this fill, and Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Record_TEMPLATE.docx, our house format for a materials acceptance record. Use the template and save the finished record as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx.

---
name: document-reading
description: How to read engineering project files quickly and reliably - the prebuilt document index, PDFs including scanned pages, drawings in DXF and PDF, spreadsheets with formulas, Word specifications, emails, IFC/BIM models - and how to extract numbers, units and scales without misreading. Use at the start of a task and whenever a document is hard to read.
---

# Reading engineering documents

## Start from the index
- `/tmp/ahpele/inventory.md`: every file with type, pages, scanned pages, revision, file-name status flags and revision
  families. `/tmp/ahpele/corpus/<path>.txt`: extracted text. Search: `grep -ril "keyword" /tmp/ahpele/corpus`.
- Read the brief/task file and the governing specification fully. Skim the rest with grep for the quantities you need.

## PDFs
- Text PDFs: use the corpus text; for tables, `pdfplumber` (`page.extract_tables()`) when available.
- Scanned pages (no text layer): open the pre-rendered PNG in `/tmp/ahpele/pages/`; if you need more detail, render
  only that page at higher resolution (pymupdf: `page.get_pixmap(dpi=200, clip=rect)`, or `pdftoppm -r 200 -f N -l N`).
  After reading an image, write what you learned (values, units, notes) to `/tmp/ahpele/notes.md`; do not re-read it.

## Drawings (DXF)
- With ezdxf: `doc = ezdxf.readfile(p); msp = doc.modelspace()`; text in TEXT/MTEXT/ATTRIB entities, dimensions in
  DIMENSION (`get_measurement()`), geometry in LINE/LWPOLYLINE/CIRCLE/INSERT; group by layer. Without ezdxf, the corpus
  text lists TEXT/MTEXT/DIMENSION/INSERT with layer and position.
- Check units ($INSUNITS header, title block, notes: feet vs metres vs inches) and the drawing scale before measuring.
- Tags, line numbers and equipment IDs on drawings link to schedules: join them explicitly in a table.

## Spreadsheets (XLSX)
- `openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=True)` gives cached values; `data_only=False` gives formulas. The corpus shows
  both (`A1=value [=formula]`). Watch for hidden sheets, merged header rows, units in header text, totals rows.

## Word (DOCX)
- `python-docx`: paragraphs and tables (`doc.tables`). Specs are organised by Part/Article/Paragraph: cite them that way.
  Look for tracked revision notes, "Rev" in headers/footers, and referenced standards with editions.

## Email (EML)
- `email` module: headers (From/To/Date/Subject), body, attachment names. Threads: order by Date.

## IFC
- `ifcopenshell.open(p)`; `f.by_type("IfcBuilding")`, property sets via `ifcopenshell.util.element.get_psets(el)`.
  If ifcopenshell is missing from the default python, look for other interpreters (`which -a python3`, virtualenvs in the
  project or /opt; `python3 -c "import ifcopenshell"` in each) before writing STEP text by hand.

## Numbers
- Record every value with its unit and source (file, page/sheet/cell, clause). Convert units explicitly in code.
- Prefer the most recent, in-force source when values conflict; note the conflict and your resolution.
=====

name: engineering-deliverables
description: Method for engineering design and calculation packages graded against requirements - document precedence, superseded documents, requirement/constraint registers, hard-constraint checks, unit discipline, optimisation within constraints, and schema-exact deliverable files (CSV, JSON, XLSX, ZIP, IFC). Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.
---

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.
- Cross-check: totals equal sums of parts, the same quantity has the same value in every file, schedules respect
  durations and predecessors, quantities respect the caps.

## 5. Build early, then improve
- Produce a complete first version of every deliverable early with conservative choices that satisfy all hard
  requirements, even if it is not optimal. An incomplete or missing file scores nothing.
- Never write placeholders (TBD, NaN, "to be determined") in a numeric field. If a value is genuinely not applicable,
  use the not-applicable convention the instruction allows (often blank, N/A or NONE).

## 6. Verify with code
- Write `/tmp/ahpele/check.py` that loads your deliverable files exactly as written and tests every requirement row and
  every checklist item (columns, tokens, units, ranges, cross-file consistency). Run it after every change.
- Run the format checker: `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <deliverable paths>`.
- For CAD/BIM outputs, re-open the file with the standard library you wrote it with and check the entities, property
  sets and attributes the instruction names.
- IFC written by hand (no BIM library): generate it with a small script, not by typing STEP lines. Copy each entity
  pattern from the example file the task provides (or from the schema), keep every attribute in order (use `$` for an
  unset one; an IfcBuildingStorey has 10 attributes, an IfcPropertySet 5, an IfcRelDefinesByProperties 6), write every REAL
  with a decimal point (`20.` or `20.0`, never `20` and never `4.5.`; coordinates, directions, depths, elevations), and double apostrophes inside strings. Run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_ifc.py <file>` until it reports 0 errors, and compare its structure printout
  (storeys and elevations, property sets, footprints, heights) with what the contract requires. One unreadable
  entity can make the whole file unreadable.
- Placed or routed 3D models (coordination models, MEP routing, layouts): verify the FILE, not your script's variables.
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_clash.py <file.ifc> --point <entry x,y,z>` re-reads it with ifcopenshell's geometry
  engine in world coordinates and lists clashing pairs, element classes stacked at one spot, broken runs and the
  distance from each run to the entry point. Coordinates in `IfcCartesianPoint` are in the project length unit (a
  millimetre project takes millimetres); library helpers such as `ifcopenshell.api` placement calls take SI metres and
  convert for you, so do not divide by 1000 by hand as well. Iterate until 0 clashes and one network per service.

## 7. Optimise last
- Only after all hard checks pass: improve the objective (cost, performance) with a systematic search (enumerate
  options, or scipy.optimize when available), re-running the checks for every candidate. Keep the best feasible plan
  on disk at all times.

SECTION 31 20 00

PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content

when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6

--- page 3 ---
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 5 ---
3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

3.8   PROTECTION
A.   Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
permanent cover.
END OF SECTION 31 20 00

Subject: Package A — Written Verification Required Before Permanent Work — Level-3 Pour and Related Items

Adrian —

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. I would appreciate a short written status against each item by end of day 07/20/2026 so that Steven and Gregory have a clean picture before the 07/22/2026 hold-point is either released or moved. If it is easier to walk me through it beforehand, I am available Monday afternoon.

Thank you.

Rachel

Subject: Package A — Level-3 Pour Readiness Notification — Placement 0530 on 07/22/2026

Adrian —

This is our formal pour-readiness notification for the Level-3 placement scheduled for 0530 on 07/22/2026. All test results for materials incorporated into this placement have been reviewed and are compliant. Specifically:

(a) Level-2 concrete 28-day cylinder reports issued 07/06/2026 — five sets, results confirm the mix.

(b) Slab-on-grade fill compaction report SF-26-0708 issued 07/09/2026 — all four tests exceed 95% requirement.

(c) Level-3 rebar lot 2026-0710 delivered 07/10/2026 — mill certificates on file (heats 4L2287, 4L2288, 4L2290, 4L2291), transmittal confirms conformance to ASTM A615/A615M-22 Grade 60.

(d) Pre-pour reinforcement and cover inspection completed 07/13/2026 — all elements comply with clear cover 1½ in per S-201.

Please issue the written verification releasing the hold-point no later than end of business 07/20/2026 so that we can confirm truck schedule with Haldenbrook.

Steven.

usage: ahpele_reqscan.py [-h] [--check] [--register REGISTER] [--limit LIMIT]
                         [--out OUT]

options:
  -h, --help           show this help message and exit
  --check              list candidates not yet adopted or rejected
  --register REGISTER  check a register file: each value must appear in the
                       document it cites

---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1


SRC_COL = re.compile(r"source|clause|document|doc\b|ref|citation|basis|standard|section", re.I)
VAL_COL = re.compile(r"value|limit|threshold|criterion|criteria|requirement|min|max|allow", re.I)
CLAUSE_REF = re.compile(r"(§\s*[\w.()-]+|\b(?:clause|section|sec\.|para\.?|table|article|art\.)\s*[\w.()-]+)", re.I)


def norm_num(x):
    x = x.replace(",", "")

GENERAL FOUNDATION NOTES
1. This sheet shows foundation systems for Blocks A, B, and C beneath the shared podium slab. Refer to sheet S-201
for typical foundation details, reinforcement schedules, and standard sections. Refer to architectural sheet A-501 for
below-grade waterproofing details at foundation walls, wall-to-mat construction joints, and slab-on-grade terminations.
2. All elevations shown are U.S. Survey Feet referenced to project datum NAVD 88. Design finished floor of the podium
level (top of structure) at El. 750.0.
3. Concrete: f'c = 5,000 psi at 28 days, Mix Design 03-CD-A. Reinforcing steel: ASTM A706/A706M Grade 60. Clear
cover per ACI 318-19 Table 20.5.1.3 durability provisions — see Spec 03 20 00 Article 3.2.
4. All dimensions to be verified in field by Contractor prior to placement. Do not scale drawings.
5. Foundation subgrades to be inspected and accepted by the Geotechnical Consultant prior to placement of blinding
concrete or reinforcement.
BLOCKS A & B — BASEMENT MAT
Extent: Continuous mat beneath Block A and Block B footprints, grids B–L / 1–5.
Underside of mat: El. 731.5. Thickness: 3.0 ft. Top of mat: El. 734.5.
Concrete: f'c = 5,000 psi, Mix 03-CD-A.
Reinforcement: see S-201/1 and S-201/2, typical mat reinforcement.
Blinding concrete: 3 in min. lean-mix, f'c = 2,000 psi, under mat.
Construction joints: permitted at grid lines B-2, F-2, K-5 only (see A-501 for waterproofing).
Mat pour dated 01/12/2026 (Block A / Block B basement extent). See progress record.
BLOCK B — PLANT-ROOM EXCAVATION (FUTURE)
Outlined on plan within Block B footprint between grids H–L / 3–5 for information. Excavation to be performed under a
separate work package following completion of the mat above.
Plan area outline: see dashed boundary on this sheet.
Subgrade elevation: El. 726.0.
Excavation depth below existing grade: 24 ft.
Temporary support of excavation: delegated design by Kesterline Engineering, PC — see shoring drawings.
Groundwater control: per Contractor's Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan (Rev.1).
Excavation scheduled start: 08/10/2026.
Extent shown for coordination only. This sheet does not release excavation for construction. Refer to S-201/4 for typical
plant-room boundary section and cutoff wall interface.
BLOCK B — PILE GROUP
Deep foundation supporting Block B basement mat and podium loads.
Pile type: closed-end pipe piles, driven.
Pile count: 48. Pile diameter: 16-in OD. Nominal length: 62 ft.
Tip elevation range: El. 686 to El. 690 (bearing in dense sand and gravel stratum below El. 720.0).
Design service load: 180 kips per pile.
Working grade at installation: El. 750.0.
Installation dates: 11/06/2025 – 11/21/2025.
Pile layout: see dot pattern on Block B plan (grids B–L / 1–5). Spacing, caps, reinforcement — see S-201/3 (typical pile
cap) and S-201/6 (pile cap group).
Pile driving records: Rowan Bay Constructors submittal package. Capacity basis: SEOR calculations (Calloway
Braddock).
BLOCK C — SPREAD FOOTINGS
Block C is founded on spread footings bearing above compressible clay. No basement is constructed beneath Block C.
Foundation type: isolated and combined spread footings.
Bearing stratum: upper sand / topsoil-stripped clay per Geotechnical Report.
Design bearing pressure: see typical spread footing S-201/3.
Bottom-of-footing elevation: varies — see typical spread footing S-201/3.
Column grid: B–L / 6–8.
Concrete: f'c = 5,000 psi, Mix 03-CD-A. Reinforcement: see S-201/5.
Settlement monitoring per project settlement monitoring plan. Refer to Block C settlement calculations and monitoring
log for status.
COLUMN GRID
Overall grid extent: transverse grid lines B, C, D, E, F, G, H, J, K, L and longitudinal grid lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8. Grid
locations.
REFERENCE NOTES
• See S-201 for typical foundation details, including mat section (S-201/1), mat reinforcement (S-201/2), pile cap
(S-201/3), construction joint and waterstop (S-201/4), and mat edge thickening (S-201/5). Cover requirements are
given in Spec 03 20 00 Article 3.2.
• See A-501 for below-grade waterproofing details at wall-to-mat construction joints (B-2, F-2, K-5), foundation drainage
terminations, and perimeter drainage board specification.
• See S-310 for podium framing plan above.
• See project Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (dated 02/14/2025) for subsurface profile, water table, and
bearing parameters.
• See Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1 for permitted dewatering extent.

PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content
31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6

--- page 2 ---
when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 3 ---
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 5 ---
3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

3.8   PROTECTION
A.   Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
permanent cover.

Item 054 is on the Package A verification list required by 07/20/2026. The question is whether Tests FD-14 through FD-17 and the supporting testing record demonstrate compliance with Specification Section 31 20 00, Article 3.4.B, and whether the fill may be built on.
9 [None] Determination: REJECTED. Against the 128.4 pcf D1557 values carried on the fill log, all four test locations pass the density criterion, but FD-14 (Grid B-3) and FD-17 (Grid G-2) fail the independent moisture criterion. The report also uses ASTM D698 Method A on the Wexford Ridge Phase 1 borrow as its reference Proctor, whereas the governing specification requires ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed. The reported compaction percentages (103.6% to 106.3%) and “PASS” dispositions therefore do not apply to this fill. Lift 6 is not accepted and no permanent work may be placed on it until the actions in Section 5 are complete.
11 [None] 2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
12 [None] The following documents were reviewed. Dates and revisions are as stated on the document. No superseded revision was used as a basis.
15 [None] 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
16 [None] Governing specification. Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025), governs. Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill. Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) expressly limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) requires, at every test location, dry density of not less than 95% of the D1557 Method C maximum dry density for the placed material and moisture content within −1% to +2% of the D1557 optimum. Article 3.4.D (p.5) makes the two criteria independent: density alone, or moisture alone, cannot establish acceptance. Article 3.7.B (p.5) requires each report to identify the D1557 denominators, measured dry density and moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation and an accept/reject disposition; Article 3.7.C (p.5) requires rework where the denominators used do not correspond to the material actually placed.
17 [None] Acceptance limits produced. The D1557 Method C values on file are 128.4 pcf maximum dry density and 9.2% optimum moisture content (VMT-25-0918-P04, Result Summary, p.3; also carried on the Block A fill log, Cover B24 and Note 5). Those values produce the following limits:

The basis is established by: (1) Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 1.3.E, 1.4.C, 2.1.A/D, 3.4.B/D and 3.7.B/C; (2) the sealed D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025, which states that its 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values supersede any earlier Proctor result for Package A structural fill and that acceptance shall be evaluated against those values under Article 3.4.B (pp.3–4); (3) the Contractor’s Block A fill log RB-FPR-BA-2026, which carries the same 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values, identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, and records the 11,400 sf pad and Lift 6 at El. 748.6 (Cover B22–B24, B30–B31; Notes 4–5; Daily Log row 24); (4) Verification Register Item 012 (D1557 result on file, closed 09/22/2025) and Item 027 (both density and moisture criteria bind independently, closed 03/13/2026); and (5) Geotechnical Report Rev.2 page 20, which states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. The D698/Wexford Ridge report does not establish the basis for this fill: it is a different test method, a different borrow source, and a material (CL-ML, 68% passing the No. 200 sieve, PI 11) that would not meet the Article 2.1.B structural-fill limits of 12% maximum passing No. 200 and PI 6 maximum.

22 [None] Each finding cites the document and page it rests on. The recomputation of the four tests is set out in Table 1 at Finding 3.
23 [None] Finding 1 — The governing acceptance standard is ASTM D1557 Method C, not ASTM D698. Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill; Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) sets the 95% density and −1%/+2% moisture criteria against that D1557 result. Verification Register Item 027 (closed 03/13/2026) confirms both criteria bind independently. Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), page 20, states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. The Block A slab-on-grade fill is structural fill under Article 1.3.A, not common fill under Article 2.2.A, so Article 3.4.B applies.
24 [None] Finding 2 — SF-26-0708 is reported against the wrong standard and the wrong borrow, and it omits the moisture criterion. Report SF-26-0708 §3 (p.1) identifies ASTM D698 Method A, maximum dry density 118.6 pcf, optimum moisture 12.1%, Curve of Record VMT-2024-0403-P1B. That curve is for the Wexford Ridge Phase 1 off-site borrow (VMT-2024-0403-P1B, p.1), a CL-ML silty clay with 68% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 11 (pp.1–2). That material does not meet Spec 31 20 00 Article 2.1.B (p.3), which limits structural fill to 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 6. The D1557 report for Package A structural fill is a different material: well-graded silty sand and gravel, USCS SM/SW-SM, 9.4% passing the No. 200 sieve and non-plastic (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1). The 103.6% to 106.3% compaction values in SF-26-0708 are computed against 118.6 pcf and are not valid against the 128.4 pcf D1557 value. The report also recites only the density requirement in §4 (p.1), has no moisture-deviation or moisture pass/fail column in §5 (pp.1–2), and accepts the fill “for density” in §6 (p.2). That is contrary to Spec 3.4.D (p.5) and the reporting requirements of 3.7.B (p.5).
25 [None] Finding 3 — Re-evaluated against the D1557 Method C values, density passes at all four locations, but moisture fails at FD-14 and FD-17. Table 1 recomputes each result. The correct percent compaction is dry density ÷ 128.4 × 100; the correct moisture deviation is measured moisture minus 9.2%.
26 [None] Table 1 — Tests FD-14 through FD-17 recomputed against ASTM D1557 Method C (128.4 pcf, 9.2%). Inputs from SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; D1557 values from VMT-25-0918-P04 p.3.
28 [None] FD-14 is 6.1% moisture, 3.1 percentage points below optimum and 2.1 points below the 8.2% lower limit. FD-17 is 5.8%, 3.4 points below optimum and 2.4 points below the lower limit. FD-15 (9.8%) and FD-16 (10.4%) are within 8.2% to 11.2% and pass both criteria. The density margin at FD-16 is thin: 122.9 pcf is 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point) above the 121.98 pcf minimum. Under Spec 3.4.B and 3.4.D (pp.4–5), both criteria must be satisfied at each location; under 3.4.C.3 (p.5), failing results may not be averaged with passing results. Lift 6 therefore fails acceptance as tested.
29 [None] Finding 4 — The number and distribution of Lift 6 tests satisfy the frequency requirement, but the record covers only Lift 6. The pad area is 11,400 sf (Fill Log Cover B22; Notes 1; Daily Log row 24). At one test per 5,000 sf, 11,400/5,000 = 2.28, so three tests per lift are required; Article 3.7.A.1 also sets a floor of three tests per lift. Four tests were taken — FD-14 at Grid B-3, FD-15 at Grid D-5, FD-16 at Grid F-4 and FD-17 at Grid G-2 — all at El. 748.6 in Lift 6 (SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; Fill Log Daily Log row 24). The frequency requirement is met with one test to spare. The log shows six lifts from El. 745.0 to El. 748.6, 3.6 ft total, at 8 in loose / 7.2 in compacted per lift (Cover B18–B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the 8 in Lift 6 thickness is within the 12 in limit. Lift 6 was placed in clear weather at 71–84 °F with no precipitation (Daily Log row 24), and no frozen material is recorded, consistent with Article 3.3.D. RFI 065 (response 09/22/2025) states one test per 500 sf; that earlier response conflicts with Rev.3 and is superseded by the later specification. I applied Rev.3’s 5,000 sf / minimum three per lift. The other five lifts are outside SF-26-0708 and are addressed in Finding 7.
30 [None] Finding 5 — The testing was performed by the Owner’s independent laboratory with a calibrated gauge, but the report and record have gaps that prevent it from being a complete acceptance document. The report is sealed by Talia Brennard, PE (p.2), and is authentic as a Vantree document; the deficiencies are technical. The D1557 report states that the Laboratory is contracted to the Owner (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 3), consistent with Spec 1.4.A. SF-26-0708 shows Vantree as the testing laboratory, Thornbury State University as client, a Troxler Model 3440 gauge (serial 34-047162), calibration dated 02/06/2026, standard counts of 2,478 density / 738 moisture, site standardization on 07/08/2026 before the first test, 60-second counts and ASTM D6938 direct transmission (p.1). On the face of the report this satisfies the calibration and daily standard-count requirements of Spec 1.4.B (p.2). However: (a) the calibration certificate is only “on file” and was not provided; (b) there is no record of the operator’s current radiation-safety training or documented competence in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures, required by 1.4.B; (c) the probe depth is 6 in while the compacted lift is 7.2 in (Fill Log Cover B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the bottom 1.2 in of the lift was not sampled and full-thickness compliance under 3.3.C is not demonstrated; (d) the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated; and (e) as found in Finding 2, it reports density only and against the wrong D698 reference. These are record deficiencies, not merely presentation issues.
31 [None] Finding 6 — The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed, and the FD-16 density margin is too thin to absorb a different Proctor. The fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse under RFI 079 (Fill Log Cover B23; Notes 4). It carries VMT-25-0918-P04, the Larchwood Pit D1557, as the governing Proctor (Cover B24; Notes 5). The only D1557 report in the record is for Larchwood Pit (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1) and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (p.4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record, and there is no D1557 on the stockpile material. Spec 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 values to be those of the material actually placed, and 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially. The record therefore does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the correct denominator for the stockpile. That matters: FD-16 passes by only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point), so a material-specific maximum dry density higher than about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. The D1557 values used in Finding 3 are the correct method and the only D1557 on file, but they are not a substitute for the stockpile-specific determination.
32 [None] Finding 7 — The record does not demonstrate that Lifts 1 through 5 were accepted, or that the subgrade and test-strip hold points were closed with test evidence. The fill log states that Lifts 1 through 5 are covered by FDR-BA-01 through FDR-BA-05, three tests per lift (Cover B31; Notes 6), and that each lift was tested before the next was placed (Notes 6; Daily Log rows 19–23). Those five reports are not in the review record, so their density/moisture results and dispositions cannot be checked. The log also records a rework of about 1,500 sf near Grid E-4 in Lift 5 for moisture correction (Daily Log row 23); no retest result for that rework is in the record. Daily Field Report No. 143 (06/30/2026) records 0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift; the package contains no Lift 5 protection or post-rain retest record for that surface. The subgrade proof-roll is recorded only as a log statement — loaded tandem-axle dump truck, Vantree present, 06/18/2026 — with written acceptance said to be memo TPM-26-063 dated 06/18/2026 (Cover B26; Notes 2); the log does not record the 20-ton loaded tandem required by RFI 118 (response 03/09/2026), and the memo is not attached. The test strip is recorded as executed 06/19/2026, witnessed by Vantree and Thelbridge, with six passes (Cover B27; Notes 3), but no test-strip results demonstrating Article 3.4.B compliance are in the record. For Lift 6 itself, the log records six smooth-drum passes and four pneumatic/plate passes (Daily Log row 24), matching the six-pass test-strip pattern; the procedure appears to have been followed, but procedure alone does not cure the moisture failures. The log also records the Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins but not the loose thickness of those hand-compacted lifts or the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls; Article 3.4.A requires those hand lifts to be not more than 6 in and prohibits heavy equipment within 3 ft of walls before balanced backfill. Spec 1.6.A/B (p.3) and 3.4.A/C (pp.4–5) make these hold points and prior-lift acceptances prerequisites. They must be produced before the fill as a whole can be accepted, even if Lift 6 is later reworked and retested.
33 [None] Finding 8 — The open moisture RFI does not change the criteria. RFI 125, raised 07/08/2026, asks for an interpretation of the moisture criteria on SF-26-0708; the RFI log shows no response and status Open (RFI Log row RFI 125). No waiver, variance or revision to Spec 31 20 00 is in the record. The criteria of Article 3.4.B apply as written. If the Contractor disputes the nuclear moisture values, ASTM D2216 is the referee method under Article 1.2.A.4; a referee result would still be evaluated against the same 8.2% to 11.2% window. RFI 065’s earlier “one test per 500 sf” response is likewise not a basis to alter the later Rev.3 frequency; Rev.3 governs.
34 [None] Finding 9 — The Contractor’s 07/14/2026 pour-readiness statement is a density-only claim against the wrong reference; it is not acceptance evidence. The notification states that “all four tests exceed 95% requirement” (S. Kendrow email, 07/14/2026, item (b)). That statement refers only to density and is computed against the wrong D698 reference; it does not address the moisture failures at FD-14 and FD-17. It is a Contractor assertion, not test evidence, and cannot support acceptance.
36 [None] 5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
37 [None] Determination: REJECTED. This record closes the Item 054 review with a determination of REJECTED; the fill itself is not accepted. Lift 6 does not meet Specification Section 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B: FD-14 and FD-17 fail the moisture criterion, and the report’s D698/Wexford Ridge reference is not the governing basis. The passing density results at FD-15 and FD-16 do not cure the failures because acceptance is evaluated at each test location and the criteria are independent (Articles 3.4.C.3 and 3.4.D). Item 054 must not be recorded as ACCEPTED.
38 [None] Before the capillary break, slab-on-grade, MEP, or any other permanent work is placed on this fill, the following must be in hand and accepted by Thelbridge:
40 [None] Schedule and register status. Item 054 is due 07/20/2026; this record is issued 07/16/2026. The Item 054 review is closed with disposition REJECTED, but the fill remains unaccepted and the register must not show it as ACCEPTED. The 07/20/2026 date is met for the determination, not for fill acceptance: a stockpile D1557, Lift 6 rework/retest, and the Lift 1–5 records are unlikely to be complete and reviewed by 07/20/2026 unless already underway, so the Block A slab-on-grade sequence should be planned to be held. A complete resubmittal will be reviewed promptly. The 07/22/2026 Level-3 hold-point is a separate item, but the 07/20/2026 status to the Owner must report Item 054 as rejected and not cleared for construction. The capillary break itself must also satisfy Spec 31 20 00 Article 2.3 (clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve) before the slab is placed.

Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) sets the 95% density and −1%/+2% moisture criteria against that D1557 result. Verification Register Item 027 (closed 03/13/2026) confirms both criteria bind independently. Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), page 20, states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. The Block A slab-on-grade fill is structural fill under Article 1.3.A, not common fill under Article 2.2.A, so Article 3.4.B applies.

That material does not meet Spec 31 20 00 Article 2.1.B (p.3), which limits structural fill to 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 6. The 103.6% to 106.3% compaction values in SF-26-0708 are computed against 118.6 pcf and are not valid against the 128.4 pcf D1557 value. The report also recites only the density requirement in §4 (p.1), has no moisture-deviation or moisture pass/fail column in §5 (pp.1–2), and accepts the fill “for density” in §6 (p.2). That is contrary to Spec 3.4.D (p.5) and the reporting requirements of 3.7.B (p.5).

The correct percent compaction is dry density ÷ 128.4 × 100; the correct moisture deviation is measured moisture minus 9.2%.

The pad area is 11,400 sf (Fill Log Cover B22; Notes 1; Daily Log row 24). At one test per 5,000 sf, 11,400/5,000 = 2.28, so three tests per lift are required; Article 3.7.A.1 also sets a floor of three tests per lift. Four tests were taken — FD-14 at Grid B-3, FD-15 at Grid D-5, FD-16 at Grid F-4 and FD-17 at Grid G-2 — all at El. 748.6 in Lift 6 (SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; Fill Log Daily Log row 24). The log shows six lifts from El. 745.0 to El. 748.6, 3.6 ft total, at 8 in loose / 7.2 in compacted per lift (Cover B18–B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the 8 in Lift 6 thickness is within the 12 in limit. The report is sealed by Talia Brennard, PE (p.2), and is authentic as a Vantree document; the deficiencies are technical. The D1557 report states that the Laboratory is contracted to the Owner (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 3), consistent with Spec 1.4.A. However: (a) the calibration certificate is only “on file” and was not provided; (b) there is no record of the operator’s current radiation-safety training or documented competence in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures, required by 1.4.B; (c) the probe depth is 6 in while the compacted lift is 7.2 in (Fill Log Cover B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the bottom 1.2 in of the lift was not sampled and full-thickness compliance under 3.3.C is not demonstrated; (d) the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated; and (e) as found in Finding 2, it reports density only and against the wrong D698 reference. These are record deficiencies, not merely presentation issues.

The fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse under RFI 079 (Fill Log Cover B23; Notes 4). It carries VMT-25-0918-P04, the Larchwood Pit D1557, as the governing Proctor (Cover B24; Notes 5). The only D1557 report in the record is for Larchwood Pit (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1) and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (p.4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record, and there is no D1557 on the stockpile material. Spec 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 values to be those of the material actually placed, and 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially. The record therefore does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the correct denominator for the stockpile. That matters: FD-16 passes by only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point), so a material-specific maximum dry density higher than about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. The D1557 values used in Finding 3 are the correct method and the only D1557 on file, but they are not a substitute for the stockpile-specific determination.

The notification states that “all four tests exceed 95% requirement” (S. Kendrow email, 07/14/2026, item (b)). That statement refers only to density and is computed against the wrong D698 reference; it does not address the moisture failures at FD-14 and FD-17. It is a Contractor assertion, not test evidence, and cannot support acceptance.

import numpy as np
w=np.array([6.2,7.5,9.2,10.8,12.4]); d=np.array([124.8,127.1,128.4,126.7,123.5])
for deg in [2,3]:
    c=np.polyfit(w,d,deg)
    # derivative roots
    dc=np.polyder(c)
    roots=np.roots(dc)
    print(deg,c,'roots',roots)
    for r in roots:
        if np.isreal(r) and 6<r.real<13:
            print('peak',r.real,np.polyval(c,r.real))
# quadratic through all five least squares
c=np.polyfit(w,d,2)
print('vertex',-c[1]/(2*c[0]),np.polyval(c,-c[1]/(2*c[0])))
# through points 2,3,4 exactly
c2=np.polyfit(w[1:4],d[1:4],2)
print('3pt vertex',-c2[1]/(2*c2[0]),np.polyval(c2,-c2[1]/(2*c2[0])))
# check ZAV
for ww in [9.2]:
    print('zav',2.68*62.4/(1+ww/100*2.68))
# check 95% values
print('95% 128.4 =',0.95*128.4)
for dd in [124.8,123.5,122.9,126.1]:
    print(dd, dd/128.4*100, dd/118.6*100)
EOF
