#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent recomputation for Item 054 — Block A slab-on-grade fill compaction.
All inputs are taken from the project record; no value is adopted from the deliverable.
"""
from math import ceil
import csv, json, os

# ---------- Inputs from the record ----------
# Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, 03/06/2026, Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 3.4.B, 3.4.C, 3.7.A.1
D1557_REQUIRED_PCT = 95.0          # % of D1557 max dry density
MOISTURE_LOWER = -1.0              # % of optimum
MOISTURE_UPPER = 2.0               # % of optimum
MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT = 3             # Article 3.7.A.1
TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF = 5000.0     # Article 3.4.B / 3.7.A.1
MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN = 12.0           # Article 3.3.A
HAND_LIFT_IN = 6.0                 # Article 3.4.A
REPORT_HOURS = 24.0                # Article 3.7.B

# Vantree Report VMT-25-0918-P04, 09/18/2025, ASTM D1557-12(2021) Method C, Larchwood Pit
GAMMA_D_MAX = 128.4                # pcf
W_OPT = 9.2                        # %
# Vantree Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B, 04/03/2024, ASTM D698 Method A, Wexford Ridge (NOT acceptance basis)
GAMMA_D_MAX_D698 = 118.6           # pcf
W_OPT_D698 = 12.1                  # %

# Fill Placement and Grading Records — Block A Slab-on-Grade, RB-FPR-BA-2026
PAD_AREA_SF = 11400.0
LIFTS = [
    # lift, date, top El. ft, loose in, compacted in, area sf, tests taken, report
    (1, '06/22/2026', 745.6, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-01'),
    (2, '06/23/2026', 746.2, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-02'),
    (3, '06/25/2026', 746.8, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-03'),
    (4, '06/26/2026', 747.4, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-04'),
    (5, '06/30/2026', 748.0, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-05'),
    (6, '07/08/2026', 748.6, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 4, 'SF-26-0708'),
]
# Field Density Report SF-26-0708, page 1-2, tests FD-14..FD-17
TESTS = [
    # id, elev ft, location, lift, dry density pcf, moisture %, reported % vs D698, reported disposition
    ('FD-14', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid B-3', 6, 124.8, 6.1, 105.2, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-15', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid D-5', 6, 123.5, 9.8, 104.1, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-16', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid F-4', 6, 122.9, 10.4, 103.6, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-17', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid G-2', 6, 126.1, 5.8, 106.3, 'PASS'),
]
PROBE_DEPTH_IN = 6.0
REPORT_TEST_DATE = '07/08/2026'
REPORT_ISSUE_DATE = '07/09/2026'

# ---------- Derived limits ----------
REQ_DENSITY = GAMMA_D_MAX * D1557_REQUIRED_PCT / 100.0          # 121.98 pcf
MOIST_LOW = W_OPT + MOISTURE_LOWER                              # 8.2 %
MOIST_HIGH = W_OPT + MOISTURE_UPPER                             # 11.2 %
D1557_95_ROUNDED = 122.0                                        # value printed in VMT-25-0918-P04

print('ITEM 054 — INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION')
print('='*78)
print(f'D1557 Method C: gamma_d,max = {GAMMA_D_MAX:.1f} pcf, w_opt = {W_OPT:.1f} %')
print(f'Required density = {D1557_REQUIRED_PCT:.0f}% x {GAMMA_D_MAX:.1f} = {REQ_DENSITY:.2f} pcf (report rounds {D1557_95_ROUNDED:.1f} pcf)')
print(f'Acceptable moisture = {W_OPT:.1f} {MOISTURE_LOWER:+.0f}% to {W_OPT:.1f} {MOISTURE_UPPER:+.0f}% = {MOIST_LOW:.1f}% to {MOIST_HIGH:.1f}%')
print(f'D698 (not acceptance basis): gamma_d,max = {GAMMA_D_MAX_D698:.1f} pcf, w_opt = {W_OPT_D698:.1f} %')
print()

# ---------- Test-by-test recomputation ----------
print('TEST RESULTS RECOMPUTED AGAINST D1557 METHOD C')
print('-'*78)
print(f"{'Test':<6}{'DD pcf':>8}{'w %':>7}{'%comp':>8}{'density':>10}{'dw':>7}{'moisture':>10}{'overall':>10}")
results = []
for tid, elev, loc, lift, dd, w, rep_pct, rep_disp in TESTS:
    pct = dd / GAMMA_D_MAX * 100.0
    dw = w - W_OPT
    density_ok = pct >= D1557_REQUIRED_PCT
    moisture_ok = MOIST_LOW <= w <= MOIST_HIGH
    overall = 'PASS' if (density_ok and moisture_ok) else 'FAIL'
    results.append(dict(id=tid, elev=elev, loc=loc, lift=lift, dd=dd, w=w, pct=pct, dw=dw,
                        density_ok=density_ok, moisture_ok=moisture_ok, overall=overall,
                        rep_pct=rep_pct, rep_disp=rep_disp))
    print(f'{tid:<6}{dd:>8.1f}{w:>7.1f}{pct:>8.1f}{("PASS" if density_ok else "FAIL"):>10}{dw:>+7.1f}{("PASS" if moisture_ok else "FAIL"):>10}{overall:>10}')
print()
for r in results:
    check_d698 = r['dd'] / GAMMA_D_MAX_D698 * 100.0
    print(f"{r['id']}: reported {r['rep_pct']:.1f}% vs D698 {GAMMA_D_MAX_D698:.1f} pcf (recomputed {check_d698:.1f}%); "
          f"correct D1557 %comp {r['pct']:.2f}%; moisture {r['w']:.1f}% vs {MOIST_LOW:.1f}-{MOIST_HIGH:.1f}%")
print()

# ---------- Worst-case utilisation per hard limit ----------
print('WORST-CASE UTILISATION PER HARD LIMIT (<=1.0 passes)')
print('-'*78)
# density: required / actual
density_utils = [(REQ_DENSITY / r['dd'], r['id'], r['dd']) for r in results]
worst_density = max(density_utils)
print(f'Density: worst {worst_density[1]} actual {worst_density[2]:.1f} pcf, required {REQ_DENSITY:.2f} pcf -> utilisation {worst_density[0]:.4f}')
# moisture: exceedance / allowed excursion on the side exceeded (or 0 if inside)
moist_utils = []
for r in results:
    if r['w'] < MOIST_LOW:
        u = (MOIST_LOW - r['w']) / abs(MOISTURE_LOWER)
    elif r['w'] > MOIST_HIGH:
        u = (r['w'] - MOIST_HIGH) / abs(MOISTURE_UPPER)
    else:
        u = 0.0
    moist_utils.append((u, r['id'], r['w']))
worst_moist = max(moist_utils)
print(f'Moisture: worst {worst_moist[1]} actual {worst_moist[2]:.1f}%, window {MOIST_LOW:.1f}-{MOIST_HIGH:.1f}% -> utilisation {worst_moist[0]:.4f}')
# frequency, every lift
freq_rows = []
for lift, date, elev, loose, comp, area, tests, report in LIFTS:
    required = max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(area / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF))
    freq_rows.append((required / tests, lift, required, tests, report))
worst_freq = max(freq_rows)
print(f'Frequency: worst Lift {worst_freq[1]} required {worst_freq[2]} tests, provided {worst_freq[3]} -> utilisation {worst_freq[0]:.4f}')
# lift thickness, every lift
thick_rows = [(loose / MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN, lift, loose) for lift, date, elev, loose, comp, area, tests, report in LIFTS]
worst_thick = max(thick_rows)
print(f'Loose lift thickness: worst Lift {worst_thick[1]} {worst_thick[2]:.1f} in / {MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN:.0f} in -> utilisation {worst_thick[0]:.4f}')
# probe depth vs compacted thickness (full-thickness coverage indicator)
probe_cov = PROBE_DEPTH_IN / LIFTS[-1][4]
print(f'Probe depth: {PROBE_DEPTH_IN:.1f} in in a {LIFTS[-1][4]:.1f} in compacted lift -> sampled fraction {probe_cov:.3f} (bottom {LIFTS[-1][4]-PROBE_DEPTH_IN:.1f} in not sampled)')
# report timing
print(f'Report timing: tested {REPORT_TEST_DATE}, issued {REPORT_ISSUE_DATE} -> 1 day vs {REPORT_HOURS:.0f} h limit (exact hours not stated)')
# total thickness / elevation
total_in = sum(l[4] for l in LIFTS)
print(f'Lift geometry: {len(LIFTS)} lifts x {LIFTS[0][4]:.1f} in compacted = {total_in:.1f} in = {total_in/12:.2f} ft; 745.0 + {total_in/12:.2f} = {745.0+total_in/12:.1f} ft')
print()

# ---------- Acceptance conclusion ----------
failed = [r['id'] for r in results if r['overall'] == 'FAIL']
print('CONCLUSION')
print('-'*78)
print(f'Tests meeting both criteria: {[r["id"] for r in results if r["overall"]=="PASS"]}')
print(f'Tests failing one or more criteria: {failed}')
print(f'Overall Lift 6 determination: {"ACCEPTED" if not failed else "REJECTED"}')
print(f'Density passes all four; moisture fails FD-14 (dry by {MOIST_LOW-TESTS[0][5]:.1f} points) and FD-17 (dry by {MOIST_LOW-TESTS[3][5]:.1f} points).')
print()

# ---------- Check the requirement table values that are directly computable ----------
print('REQUIREMENT-TABLE CHECK (numeric limits directly applicable to Item 054)')
print('-'*78)
req_checks = {
    'REQ-041': (min(r['pct'] for r in results) >= D1557_REQUIRED_PCT, f'minimum %comp {min(r["pct"] for r in results):.2f} >= 95'),
    'REQ-042': (all(MOIST_LOW <= r['w'] <= MOIST_HIGH for r in results), f'moisture values {[r["w"] for r in results]} in {MOIST_LOW}-{MOIST_HIGH}'),
    'REQ-043': (all(r['density_ok'] and r['moisture_ok'] for r in results), 'both criteria at every test location'),
    'REQ-044': (all(t >= max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(a / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF)) for _,_,_,_,_,a,t,_ in LIFTS), 'frequency per lift'),
    'REQ-059': (all(t >= max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(a / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF)) for _,_,_,_,_,a,t,_ in LIFTS), 'frequency and minimum three per lift'),
    'REQ-031': (all(l[3] <= MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN for l in LIFTS), 'loose lift <=12 in'),
    'REQ-047': (all(r['overall'] == 'PASS' for r in results), 'retest not available; original failing locations not both passing'),
}
for rid,(ok,desc) in req_checks.items():
    print(f'{rid}: {"PASS" if ok else "FAIL"} — {desc}')
print()
print('Non-numeric/record checks (addressed in the acceptance record):')
print('- REQ-003/004: D698 not acceptance basis; D1557 governs — report uses D698, so reporting basis is nonconforming.')
print('- REQ-014/015: D1557 on material actually placed at each location — only Larchwood Pit D1557 on file; stockpile north of Block C not tested.')
print('- REQ-019/062: report must give D1557 denominators, moisture deviation and dual disposition — SF-26-0708 does not.')
print('- REQ-020/071: written subgrade proof-roll acceptance — memo TPM-26-063 cited but not in review record.')
print('- REQ-037: test strip must demonstrate criteria — log records test strip but no test results on file.')
print('- REQ-061: report within 24 h — next-day issue meets date evidence but issue time is not stated.')
print('- REQ-012/013: operator training and gauge calibration — calibration date and standard counts stated; certificate/competency records not in record.')

# Write machine-readable results
os.makedirs('/tmp/ahpele/out', exist_ok=True)
json.dump(dict(limits=dict(req_density=REQ_DENSITY,moist_low=MOIST_LOW,moist_high=MOIST_HIGH,
                          gamma_d_max=GAMMA_D_MAX,w_opt=W_OPT),
               results=results, failed=failed, freq=freq_rows, lifts=LIFTS),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Self-check of the Item 054 materials acceptance record against the checklist,
the requirements table and the independent recomputation."""
import csv, json, os, re, sys
from docx import Document

DOCX='/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx'
REQ='/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv'
VER='/tmp/ahpele/out/verify_results.json'
fails=[]; notes=[]

def fail(msg): fails.append(msg)
def ok(msg): notes.append(msg)

if not os.path.exists(DOCX):
    print('FAIL: deliverable missing',DOCX); sys.exit(1)
d=Document(DOCX)
paras=[p.text.strip() for p in d.paragraphs]
doc_text='\n'.join(paras)
table_text=[]
for t in d.tables:
    for r in t.rows:
        table_text.append(' | '.join(c.text.strip() for c in r.cells))
all_text=doc_text+'\n'+'\n'.join(table_text)
flat=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',all_text)

# ---------- 1. Template structure ----------
ok('DOCX opens with python-docx: %d paragraphs, %d tables' % (len(paras),len(d.tables)))
for s in ['THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES','MATERIALS ACCEPTANCE RECORD']:
    if s not in doc_text: fail('missing template header: '+s)
headings=['1.  PURPOSE','2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED','3.  BASIS OF REVIEW','4.  FINDINGS','5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION']
pos=[]
for h in headings:
    found=[i for i,p in enumerate(paras) if p.strip().startswith(h)]
    if not found: fail('missing section heading: '+h)
    else: pos.append(found[0])
if pos != sorted(pos): fail('section headings are not in template order: %s' % pos)
for label in ['To:','From:','Date:','Subject:']:
    if not any(p.startswith(label) for p in paras): fail('missing field '+label)
for s in ['Karen Tarbray','Materials / QA Reviewer','Thelbridge Project Management Services - Owner\'s Representative','07/16/2026']:
    if s not in doc_text: fail('signature block missing: '+s)

# ---------- 2. Required content / asks ----------
checks={
 'Item 054':'Item 054 identification',
 'SF-26-0708':'field density report number',
 'FD-14':'test FD-14','FD-15':'test FD-15','FD-16':'test FD-16','FD-17':'test FD-17',
 '31 20 00':'governing specification',
 'ASTM D1557':'D1557 basis','ASTM D698':'D698 rejected basis',
 '128.4 pcf':'D1557 maximum dry density','9.2%':'D1557 optimum moisture',
 '121.98 pcf':'95% density limit','8.2%':'lower moisture limit','11.2%':'upper moisture limit',
 '11,400 sf':'pad area','5,000 sf':'test frequency','three tests per lift':'minimum tests per lift',
 '8 in':'loose lift thickness','12 in':'maximum loose lift','7.2 in':'compacted lift thickness',
 '07/08/2026':'test date','07/09/2026':'report issue date','07/20/2026':'register due date',
 'REJECTED':'REJECTED determination',
 'FD-14':'FD-14 result','FD-17':'FD-17 result',
}
for s,desc in checks.items():
    if s not in flat: fail('missing %s (%r)' % (desc,s))
for s in ['FD-14 and FD-17 fail','FD-15','FD-16','pass both criteria','moisture criterion','rework','retest',
          'stockpile north of Block C','FDR-BA-01','FDR-BA-05','TPM-26-063','test strip','calibration',
          'operator','radiation-safety','protect the fill','capillary break','no permanent work']:
    if s.lower() not in flat.lower(): fail('missing required coverage: '+s)
if 'Determination: REJECTED' not in flat: fail('determination does not use exact ACCEPTED/REJECTED convention')
if 'must not be recorded as ACCEPTED' not in flat: fail('does not state item must not be recorded ACCEPTED')
# No template placeholders
prompts=['State the verification register item','List each document relied on','Cite the governing specification',
         'Number each finding','State the determination using ACCEPTED or REJECTED']
for bad in prompts:
    if bad.lower() in flat.lower(): fail('template prompt remains: '+bad)
for bad in ['TBD','TBA','TODO','NaN']:
    if re.search(r'\b'+re.escape(bad)+r'\b', flat, re.I): fail('placeholder token remains: '+bad)

# ---------- 3. Recompute and check the results table ----------
ver=json.load(open(VER,encoding='utf-8'))
expected={r['id']:r for r in ver['results']}
# locate results table
rt=None
for t in d.tables:
    hdr=[c.text.strip() for c in t.rows[0].cells]
    if 'Test' in hdr and 'Overall' in hdr and 'Dry density (pcf)' in hdr:
        rt=t; break
if rt is None:
    fail('results table not found')
else:
    hdr=[c.text.strip() for c in rt.rows[0].cells]
    idx={h:i for i,h in enumerate(hdr)}
    seen=set()
    for row in rt.rows[1:]:

        if abs(w-e['w'])>1e-9: fail('%s moisture %s != %s' % (tid,w,e['w']))
        if abs(pct-round(e['pct'],1))>0.05: fail('%s %%comp %s != %.2f' % (tid,pct,e['pct']))

    if seen != set(expected): fail('results table does not contain exactly FD-14..FD-17: %s' % sorted(seen))
    ok('results table parsed and matches independent recomputation for %s' % sorted(seen))

if not flat.startswith('') and '2.1 points below' not in flat: fail('FD-14 moisture exceedance not stated')

if '0.9 pcf' not in flat: fail('FD-16 density margin not stated')

# ---------- 4. Requirements table coverage ----------
reqs=list(csv.DictReader(open(REQ,encoding='utf-8')))

def has(*terms): return all(term.lower() in flat.lower() for term in terms)
status={}

status['REQ-026'] = ('PASS' if has('3/4 in') and has('2% passing') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-031'] = ('PASS' if has('8 in') and has('12 in') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-037'] = ('PASS' if has('test strip') and has('06/19/2026') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-040'] = ('PASS' if has('each lift was tested') or has('Lifts 1 through 5') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-041'] = ('PASS' if has('121.98 pcf') and has('95%') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-042'] = ('PASS' if has('8.2%') and has('11.2%') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-043'] = ('PASS' if has('both criteria') and has('each test location') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-044'] = ('PASS' if has('11,400 sf') and has('5,000 sf') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-045'] = ('PASS' if has('rework') else 'FAIL')
status['REQ-046'] = ('PASS' if has('retest') else 'FAIL')

# Independent review — Item 054 materials acceptance record

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` (DOCX, dated 07/16/2026, determination REJECTED).

**Governing documents checked:** Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025); Vantree D1557 Report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025; Vantree D698 Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B dated 04/03/2024; Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 dated 07/09/2026; Contractor Fill Placement Record RB-FPR-BA-2026; RFI Log (updated 07/13/2026); Thelbridge Verification Register (updated 07/15/2026); Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 dated 02/14/2025; house template.

**Overall result:** The final **REJECTED** determination is correct on the two moisture failures (FD-14 at 6.1% and FD-17 at 5.8%, against the 8.2%–11.2% window from 9.2% optimum). The record nevertheless contains material overstatements and omissions, principally that it reports density as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the placed stockpile material, and it omits the structural-fill material requirements of Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C. Findings are listed most serious first.

---

## 1. MAJOR — Density is reported as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the material actually placed

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2), 2.1.D (p.3), 3.4.B (p.4) and 3.4.D (p.5) require the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be those of the material actually placed at the test location; Article 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow. The task also asks “what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.”

**What the deliverable has:** Section 3 (“What in the record establishes this basis for this fill”) says the basis is established by the D1557 report and the fill log, which “carries the same 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values.” Table 1 and the Conclusion then state that density passes all four locations against 121.98 pcf, and the author’s final summary says “Density passes all four tests.” Finding 6 itself says: “The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed” and “there is no D1557 on the stockpile material.”

**What it should be:** The record should state directly that the D1557 basis for the **placed stockpile material** is not established: the only D1557 on file is for Larchwood Pit, while the Block A fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, and the RFI 079 approval was “subject to gradation retest” with letter TPM-25-079 and the retest not in the record. The 128.4 pcf / 9.2% density pass is therefore conditional and cannot be certified; the determination is REJECTED on this ground as well as on moisture. The author’s own Finding 5(c) also says the 6-in probe did not sample the bottom 1.2 in of the 7.2-in compacted lift, so full-lift density is not demonstrated even if the denominator were correct.

**Evidence / computation:**
- Fill log Cover B23: borrow source “Stockpile north of Block C — approved for reuse per RFI 079”; Cover B24: “Governing Proctor reference … VMT-25-0918-P04 … 128.4 pcf … 9.2%.”

# Independent review — Item 054 materials acceptance record

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` (DOCX, dated 07/16/2026, determination REJECTED).

**Governing documents checked:** Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025); Vantree D1557 Report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025; Vantree D698 Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B dated 04/03/2024; Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 dated 07/09/2026; Contractor Fill Placement Record RB-FPR-BA-2026; RFI Log (updated 07/13/2026); Thelbridge Verification Register (updated 07/15/2026); Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 dated 02/14/2025; house template.

**Overall result:** The final **REJECTED** determination is correct on the two moisture failures (FD-14 at 6.1% and FD-17 at 5.8%, against the 8.2%–11.2% window from 9.2% optimum). The record nevertheless contains material overstatements and omissions, principally that it reports density as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the placed stockpile material, and it omits the structural-fill material requirements of Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C. Findings are listed most serious first.

---

## 1. MAJOR — Density is reported as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the material actually placed

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2), 2.1.D (p.3), 3.4.B (p.4) and 3.4.D (p.5) require the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be those of the material actually placed at the test location; Article 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow. The task also asks “what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.”

**What the deliverable has:** Section 3 (“What in the record establishes this basis for this fill”) says the basis is established by the D1557 report and the fill log, which “carries the same 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values.” Table 1 shows density PASS at all four locations against 121.98 pcf, the Purpose/Determination paragraph says “all four test locations pass the density criterion,” and the author’s final summary says “Density passes all four tests.” Finding 6 itself says: “The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed” and “there is no D1557 on the stockpile material.”

**What it should be:** The record should state directly that the D1557 basis for the **placed stockpile material** is not established: the only D1557 on file is for Larchwood Pit, while the Block A fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, and the RFI 079 approval was “subject to gradation retest” with letter TPM-25-079 and the retest not in the record. The 128.4 pcf / 9.2% density pass is therefore conditional and cannot be certified; the determination is REJECTED on this ground as well as on moisture. The author’s own Finding 5(c) also says the 6-in probe did not sample the bottom 1.2 in of the 7.2-in compacted lift, so full-lift density is not demonstrated even if the denominator were correct.

**Evidence / computation:**
- Fill log Cover B23: borrow source “Stockpile north of Block C — approved for reuse per RFI 079”; Cover B24: “Governing Proctor reference … VMT-25-0918-P04 … 128.4 pcf … 9.2%.”
- D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 p.1: borrow source “Larchwood Pit — Package A structural fill”; p.4 Note 4: “This report pertains only to the sample tested.”
- RFI Log row RFI 079 (10/10/2025): “Approved subject to gradation retest; see letter TPM-25-079.” No TPM-25-079 and no stockpile D1557 are in the record.
- Recomputed percentages against 128.4 pcf: FD-14 124.8/128.4 = 97.2%; FD-15 123.5/128.4 = 96.2%; FD-16 122.9/128.4 = 95.7%; FD-17 126.1/128.4 = 98.2%. All are above 95% **only if 128.4 pcf is the correct maximum for the placed material**. FD-16’s margin is only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point); a stockpile maximum above 129.4 pcf would fail FD-16.

---

## 2. MAJOR — The structural-fill material requirements of Article 2.1.A/B/C are not verified or required for the stockpile

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 2.1.A (p.3): well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM; Article 2.1.B (p.3): no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI not exceeding 6; Article 2.1.C (p.3): free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension. Article 1.5.A.1 also requires source identification including gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification before placement.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 2 applies Article 2.1.B only to the **D698/Wexford Ridge** material (68% passing No. 200, PI 11) and does not apply Articles 2.1.A/B/C to the stockpile actually placed. Action 3 asks for “gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification per Article 1.5.A.1” but does not state the Article 2.1.A/B/C acceptance criteria or require a deleterious/particle-size inspection. The deliverable never mentions the 3-inch limit, organic material, or debris; “frozen” appears only in the Article 3.3.D placement sentence (“no frozen material is recorded”), not as a material-acceptance check under Article 2.1.C. Table 1’s limits also omit the material criteria. The author’s own `requirements.csv` includes REQ-022/REQ-023/REQ-024 as applying to “All structural fill,” but the author’s `check.py` maps REQ-024 to “REF” and the DOCX does not address it.

**What it should be:** The record should require, as a condition before the fill is accepted, that the stockpile north of Block C be tested/classified against Article 2.1.A/B/C: USCS SM or SW-SM; ≤12% passing No. 200; PI ≤6; no organic material, frozen soil, debris, or particles >3 in. It should state these limits in the Basis/limits table and require the results in the action table.

**Evidence:**
- Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 p.3, Articles 2.1.A–C (quoted above).
- D1557 report p.1 describes the Larchwood Pit sample as “well-graded silty sand and gravel with occasional cobbles”; the report does not quantify the cobble size or demonstrate the 3-in limit.
- D698 report p.1–2: Wexford Ridge CL-ML, 68% passing No. 200, PI 11 — fails Article 2.1.B, but it is not the stockpile.
- Fill log Cover B23–B24: stockpile north of Block C; no gradation, Atterberg, USCS or deleterious record for that stockpile; RFI 079 retest missing.
- DOCX text search: no occurrence of “3 in”, “3 inches”, “organic”, “deleterious”, “particles”, or “debris”; “frozen” occurs once, in the Article 3.3.D weather sentence.

---

## 3. MAJOR — The 24-hour report-issue requirement of Article 3.7.B is treated as satisfied when the record does not demonstrate it

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.7.B (p.5): “The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing.”

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 5(d): “the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated.”

**What it should be:** The record should say the 24-hour requirement is **not demonstrated** from the record. The report shows only “Date Tested: 07/08/2026” and “Date Issued: 07/09/2026” (SF-26-0708 p.1); the field work ended at 11:30 on 07/08 (arrival/departure 07:15/11:30, p.1). Any issue after 11:30 on 07/09 would exceed 24 hours, and no issue time is recorded. The report should be reissued with the issue time or the Laboratory should confirm the time.

**Evidence:** SF-26-0708 p.1 dates and arrival/departure; p.2 signature date 07/09/2026; no time of issue anywhere in the report.

---

## 4. MAJOR — The daily standard-count / calibration / operator-competency requirements of Article 1.4.B are not established, although the deliverable says they are satisfied “on the face of the report”

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 1.4.B (p.2): nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation-safety training and be documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures; gauges shall be calibrated within the manufacturer’s stated interval and standard-count checked at the start of each testing day.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 5 says: “On the face of the report this satisfies the calibration and daily standard-count requirements of Spec 1.4.B (p.2).” It then lists (a) the calibration certificate was not provided and (b) no operator radiation-safety training/competence record. Action 7 requires “the gauge calibration certificate, daily standard-count record and operator radiation-safety training / D6938 competency records.”

**What it should be:** The report’s 2,478 density / 738 moisture values are the **reference standard counts** in the Equipment table, not the daily standard-count readings; the report only states that standardization was performed and results were within manufacturer tolerance. The certificate, the daily count readings and the operator records are absent. The record should say these requirements are **not verified** until the documents in action 7 are produced, not that the report satisfies them on its face.

**Evidence:** SF-26-0708 p.1 §2 (gauge, serial, calibration date, standard counts, probe depth, count time, standardization statement); no certificate, daily count sheet or operator training record in the corpus; DOCX Finding 5 and action 7 as quoted.

---

## 5. MAJOR — The record does not establish whether Article 3.5 (backfill against walls) or Article 3.6 (settlement) applies; both are treated as not applicable without support

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.5.A/B/C (p.5): backfill against basement/foundation walls only after the wall attains 28-day strength or permanent lateral support; balanced lifts on both sides of interior walls; compact backfill to Article 3.4.B where it supports structure or slabs. Article 3.6 (p.5): total settlement 1.0 in maximum, differential 0.5 in over 30 ft, with notification before additional load.

**What the deliverable has:** No mention of Article 3.5 or 3.6. Finding 7 mentions “Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins,” “hand-compacted lifts,” and “the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls,” which shows walls are adjacent, but it applies only Article 3.4.A. The author’s `check.py` maps REQ-052–REQ-054 (Article 3.5) and REQ-055–REQ-058 (Article 3.6) to “N/A.”

**What it should be:** The record should either (a) establish that the fill is not backfill against the basement walls (and that Article 3.5 does not apply), or (b) apply Article 3.5.A/B/C and require the wall-strength/balanced-lift records. It should also state whether the Article 3.6 settlement criteria are part of the fill acceptance or are covered by a separate item; the fill is under a slab-on-grade and the record cannot simply omit the section’s settlement tolerance.

**Evidence:** Fill log Cover B29 (Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins) and Finding 7’s own “3-ft … setback from walls”; Sheet S-201 Detail 1/S-201: basement wall extends to underside of podium slab at El. 748.5; fill log finish grade El. 748.6. The DOCX contains no “3.5” article citation, no “settlement,” and no “1.0 in / 0.5 in.”

---

## 6. MINOR — The D1557 report’s own curve-fit statement does not reproduce 128.4 pcf at 9.2%; the fitted peak is about 128.2 pcf at 9.04%

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.4.B (p.4) uses the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content.

**What the deliverable has:** 128.4 pcf maximum and 9.2% optimum, giving 121.98 pcf and 8.2%–11.2%.

**What it should be:** The Proctor report p.3 says “Curve fit: second-order polynomial through the five primary data points; peak located by first-derivative solution.” A least-squares quadratic through the five points (6.2/124.8, 7.5/127.1, 9.2/128.4, 10.8/126.7, 12.4/123.5) peaks at **128.20 pcf at 9.04%**, not 128.4/9.2; 128.4 pcf is the highest measured point. The exact 95% of the fitted peak would be 121.79 pcf and the moisture window 8.04%–11.04%. The pass/fail outcome does not change (FD-16 122.9 still passes; FD-14/FD-17 still fail), but the stated limits are not exactly the fitted peak and should be confirmed with the Laboratory.

**Evidence:** D1557 report p.2 data points; p.3 curve-fit statement and plot; independent least-squares calculation (quadratic coefficients [-0.4224, 7.6400, 93.6551], vertex at 9.0429%, 128.199 pcf).

---

## 7. MINOR — The 0.42 in of rain overnight into 07/01/2026 is omitted from the Lift 5 protection/retest discussion

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.8.A (p.6): protect completed structural fill from softening by precipitation; rework and retest any area disturbed or softened.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 7 cites only “0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift on 06/30/2026” and action 5 requires protection/retest after that event.

**What it should be:** Daily Field Report No. 144 (07/01/2026) records “0.42 in overnight (per gate gauge), trace during shift” into 07/01, after the Lift 5 placement on 06/30 and before the Lift 6 placement on 07/08. That larger event should also be included in the Lift 5 protection/retest requirement.

**Evidence:** Daily Field Reports pp.3–4, Report No. 143 (0.35 in overnight 06/30) and Report No. 144 (0.42 in overnight into 07/01).

---

## 8. MINOR — The D698 report is called the “wrong borrow” without evidence that the stockpile is not Wexford Ridge material

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1): ASTM D698 is historical borrow characterization only and not the acceptance basis; Article 2.1.B (p.3): structural fill limits.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 2 and the Documents Reviewed table call the D698/Wexford Ridge report a “different borrow source” and “wrong method and different borrow/material.”

**What it should be:** The D698 report is not the acceptance basis because it is the wrong test method and its material (CL-ML, 68% passing No. 200, PI 11) does not meet Article 2.1.B. The record does not, however, establish that the stockpile north of Block C is not Wexford Ridge Phase 1 material; the fill log does not state the stockpile’s origin, and the RFI 079 letter/retest is missing. The finding should not assert a different borrow as a fact.

**Evidence:** Fill log Cover B23 (stockpile north of Block C, no origin); D698 report p.1 (Wexford Ridge Phase 1 off-site borrow); no document tying or separating the two.

---

## 9. MINOR — The RFI 065 “one test per 500 sf” response is treated as superseded without an explicit supersession

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 3.4.B and 3.7.A.1 (pp.4–5): one test per 5,000 sf per lift and not fewer than three tests per lift.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 4 applies 5,000 sf / three tests and says RFI 065’s “one test per 500 sf” response “conflicts with Rev.3 and is superseded by the later specification.”

**What it should be:** The current Rev.3 text supports 5,000 sf / three tests, but the record contains no explicit statement that Rev.2/Rev.3 superseded RFI 065 (answered 09/22/2025 under the earlier revision). If RFI 065 still governed, 11,400 sf would require 23 tests per lift, not 4, and the frequency conclusion would fail. The record should cite the revision history or obtain an RFI confirmation; it should not simply assert supersession.

**Evidence:** RFI Log row RFI 065 (09/22/2025); Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 revision history (Rev.2 11/14/2025 “Article 3.4 restructured”; Rev.3 03/06/2026 “Article 3.4.B acceptance criteria clarified”); no ASI/change order in the corpus.

---

## 10. MINOR — The Geotechnical Report page citation is to PDF page 20, but the report’s printed page is 19

**Requirement:** Citation accuracy; the task requires each finding to cite the document and page it rests on.

**What the deliverable has:** “Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), page 20” (Finding 1; Documents Reviewed table “Page 20”).

**What it should be:** The 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% text is on PDF page 20 of the 21-page file, but the report’s own footer on that page is “Page 19.” The citation should say “PDF p.20 / report p.19” or similar.

**Evidence:** Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, PDF page marker `--- page 20 ---`, footer “Page 19”; text at lines 878–882.

---

## 11. MINOR — The action for failing tests does not state that rework is at the Contractor’s expense

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.4.C.1 (p.5): the affected area shall be reworked “at the Contractor’s expense.”

**What the deliverable has:** Action 1: “Rework and retest Lift 6 at FD-14 … and FD-17 …” with owner “Rowan Bay / Vantree”; no expense statement.

**What it should be:** Add “at the Contractor’s expense” to action 1, consistent with Article 3.4.C.1.

**Evidence:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 p.5 Article 3.4.C.1; DOCX action table row 1.

---

## 12. MINOR — The “limits it produces” table omits the material, hold-point and protection limits that the findings rely on

**Requirement:** Task instruction: “State the acceptance basis you are using, the limits it produces, and what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.” Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C, 1.6.A/B, 3.3.A/B/D, 3.4.A, 3.8.A.

**What the deliverable has:** Table 1 lists reference standard, dry density, moisture, both criteria, frequency, lift thickness, reporting and nonconforming work. It does not list the Article 2.1.A/B/C material limits, the Article 1.6.A/B proof-roll/prior-lift hold points, the Article 3.4.A hand-lift/setback limits, or the Article 3.8.A protection requirement, although some appear in Findings 5/7 and the action table.

**What it should be:** Add these limits to Table 1 or cross-reference the findings so the reader can see the complete set of acceptance limits in one place.

## 13. MINOR — The register status is ambiguous: “review is closed” while the fill remains unaccepted

**Requirement:** Register conventions: status values Open/Closed/Closed-w-Comment; materials dispositions ACCEPTED/REJECTED. The task says Item 054 has to close before 07/20/2026.

**What the deliverable has:** “This record closes the Item 054 review with a determination of REJECTED; the fill itself is not accepted” and “Item 054 must not be recorded as ACCEPTED.”

**What it should be:** State the register entry explicitly: Item 054 status **Closed** with disposition **REJECTED**, plus a new/revised item for the Lift 6 rework/retest and material qualification. The current wording leaves the reader unsure whether the register item is closed or still open.

# Independent review — Item 054 materials acceptance record

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` (DOCX, dated 07/16/2026, determination REJECTED).

**Governing documents checked:** Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025); Vantree D1557 Report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025; Vantree D698 Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B dated 04/03/2024; Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 dated 07/09/2026; Contractor Fill Placement Record RB-FPR-BA-2026; RFI Log (updated 07/13/2026); Thelbridge Verification Register (updated 07/15/2026); Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 dated 02/14/2025; house template.

**Overall result:** The final **REJECTED** determination is correct on the two moisture failures (FD-14 at 6.1% and FD-17 at 5.8%, against the 8.2%–11.2% window from 9.2% optimum). The record nevertheless contains material overstatements and omissions, principally that it reports density as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the placed stockpile material, and it omits the structural-fill material requirements of Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C. Findings are listed most serious first.

---

## 1. MAJOR — Density is reported as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the material actually placed

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2), 2.1.D (p.3), 3.4.B (p.4) and 3.4.D (p.5) require the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be those of the material actually placed at the test location; Article 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow. The task also asks “what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.”

**What the deliverable has:** Section 3 (“What in the record establishes this basis for this fill”) says the basis is established by the D1557 report and the fill log, which “carries the same 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values.” Table 1 shows density PASS at all four locations against 121.98 pcf, the Purpose/Determination paragraph says “all four test locations pass the density criterion,” and the author’s final summary says “Density passes all four tests.” Finding 6 itself says: “The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed” and “there is no D1557 on the stockpile material.”

**What it should be:** The record should state directly that the D1557 basis for the **placed stockpile material** is not established: the only D1557 on file is for Larchwood Pit, while the Block A fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, and the RFI 079 approval was “subject to gradation retest” with letter TPM-25-079 and the retest not in the record. The 128.4 pcf / 9.2% density pass is therefore conditional and cannot be certified; the determination is REJECTED on this ground as well as on moisture. The author’s own Finding 5(c) also says the 6-in probe did not sample the bottom 1.2 in of the 7.2-in compacted lift, so full-lift density is not demonstrated even if the denominator were correct.

**Evidence / computation:**
- Fill log Cover B23: borrow source “Stockpile north of Block C — approved for reuse per RFI 079”; Cover B24: “Governing Proctor reference … VMT-25-0918-P04 … 128.4 pcf … 9.2%.”
- D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 p.1: borrow source “Larchwood Pit — Package A structural fill”; p.4 Note 4: “This report pertains only to the sample tested.”
- RFI Log row RFI 079 (10/10/2025): “Approved subject to gradation retest; see letter TPM-25-079.” No TPM-25-079 and no stockpile D1557 are in the record.
- Recomputed percentages against 128.4 pcf: FD-14 124.8/128.4 = 97.2%; FD-15 123.5/128.4 = 96.2%; FD-16 122.9/128.4 = 95.7%; FD-17 126.1/128.4 = 98.2%. All are above 95% **only if 128.4 pcf is the correct maximum for the placed material**. FD-16’s margin is only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point); a stockpile maximum above 129.4 pcf would fail FD-16.

---

## 2. MAJOR — The structural-fill material requirements of Article 2.1.A/B/C are not verified or required for the stockpile

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 2.1.A (p.3): well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM; Article 2.1.B (p.3): no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI not exceeding 6; Article 2.1.C (p.3): free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension. Article 1.5.A.1 also requires source identification including gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification before placement.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 2 applies Article 2.1.B only to the **D698/Wexford Ridge** material (68% passing No. 200, PI 11) and does not apply Articles 2.1.A/B/C to the stockpile actually placed. Action 3 asks for “gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification per Article 1.5.A.1” but does not state the Article 2.1.A/B/C acceptance criteria or require a deleterious/particle-size inspection. ## 5. MINOR — The record does not establish whether Article 3.5 (backfill against walls) or Article 3.6 (settlement) applies; both are treated as not applicable without support

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.5.A/B/C (p.5): backfill against basement/foundation walls only after the wall attains 28-day strength or permanent lateral support; balanced lifts on both sides of interior walls; compact backfill to Article 3.4.B where it supports structure or slabs. Finding 7 mentions “Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins,” “hand-compacted lifts,” and “the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls,” which shows walls are adjacent, but it applies only Article 3.4.A. It should also state whether the Article 3.6 settlement criteria are part of the fill acceptance or are covered by a separate item; the fill is under a slab-on-grade and the record cannot simply omit the section’s settlement tolerance.

## 6. MINOR — The D1557 report’s own curve-fit statement does not reproduce 128.4 pcf at 9.2%; the fitted peak is about 128.2 pcf at 9.04%

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.4.B (p.4) uses the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content.

**What the deliverable has:** 128.4 pcf maximum and 9.2% optimum, giving 121.98 pcf and 8.2%–11.2%.

**What it should be:** The Proctor report p.3 says “Curve fit: second-order polynomial through the five primary data points; peak located by first-derivative solution.” A least-squares quadratic through the five points (6.2/124.8, 7.5/127.1, 9.2/128.4, 10.8/126.7, 12.4/123.5) peaks at **128.20 pcf at 9.04%**, not 128.4/9.2; 128.4 pcf is the highest measured point. The exact 95% of the fitted peak would be 121.79 pcf and the moisture window 8.04%–11.04%. The pass/fail outcome does not change (FD-16 122.9 still passes; FD-14/FD-17 still fail), but the stated limits are not exactly the fitted peak and should be confirmed with the Laboratory.

**Evidence:** D1557 report p.2 data points; p.3 curve-fit statement and plot; independent least-squares calculation (quadratic coefficients [-0.4224, 7.6400, 93.6551], vertex at 9.0429%, 128.199 pcf).

exit_code=0
# Independent review — Item 054 materials acceptance record

**Deliverable reviewed:** `/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx` (DOCX, dated 07/16/2026, determination REJECTED).

**Governing documents checked:** Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025); Vantree D1557 Report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025; Vantree D698 Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B dated 04/03/2024; Vantree Field Density Report SF-26-0708 dated 07/09/2026; Contractor Fill Placement Record RB-FPR-BA-2026; RFI Log (updated 07/13/2026); Thelbridge Verification Register (updated 07/15/2026); Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 dated 02/14/2025; house template.

**Overall result:** The final **REJECTED** determination is correct on the two moisture failures (FD-14 at 6.1% and FD-17 at 5.8%, against the 8.2%–11.2% window from 9.2% optimum). The record nevertheless contains material overstatements and omissions, principally that it reports density as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the placed stockpile material, and it omits the structural-fill material requirements of Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C. Findings are listed most serious first.

---

## 1. MAJOR — Density is reported as passing even though the D1557 denominator is not established for the material actually placed

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2), 2.1.D (p.3), 3.4.B (p.4) and 3.4.D (p.5) require the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be those of the material actually placed at the test location; Article 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow. The task also asks “what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.”

**What the deliverable has:** Section 3 (“What in the record establishes this basis for this fill”) says the basis is established by the D1557 report and the fill log, which “carries the same 128.4 pcf / 9.2% values.” Table 1 shows density PASS at all four locations against 121.98 pcf, the Purpose/Determination paragraph says “all four test locations pass the density criterion,” and the author’s final summary says “Density passes all four tests.” Finding 6 itself says: “The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed” and “there is no D1557 on the stockpile material.”

**What it should be:** The record should state directly that the D1557 basis for the **placed stockpile material** is not established: the only D1557 on file is for Larchwood Pit, while the Block A fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, and the RFI 079 approval was “subject to gradation retest” with letter TPM-25-079 and the retest not in the record. The 128.4 pcf / 9.2% density pass is therefore conditional and cannot be certified; the determination is REJECTED on this ground as well as on moisture. The author’s own Finding 5(c) also says the 6-in probe did not sample the bottom 1.2 in of the 7.2-in compacted lift, so full-lift density is not demonstrated even if the denominator were correct.

**Evidence / computation:**
- Fill log Cover B23: borrow source “Stockpile north of Block C — approved for reuse per RFI 079”; Cover B24: “Governing Proctor reference … VMT-25-0918-P04 … 128.4 pcf … 9.2%.”
- D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 p.1: borrow source “Larchwood Pit — Package A structural fill”; p.4 Note 4: “This report pertains only to the sample tested.”
- RFI Log row RFI 079 (10/10/2025): “Approved subject to gradation retest; see letter TPM-25-079.” No TPM-25-079 and no stockpile D1557 are in the record.
- Recomputed percentages against 128.4 pcf: FD-14 124.8/128.4 = 97.2%; FD-15 123.5/128.4 = 96.2%; FD-16 122.9/128.4 = 95.7%; FD-17 126.1/128.4 = 98.2%. All are above 95% **only if 128.4 pcf is the correct maximum for the placed material**. FD-16’s margin is only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point); a stockpile maximum above 129.4 pcf would fail FD-16.

---

## 2. MAJOR — The structural-fill material requirements of Article 2.1.A/B/C are not verified or required for the stockpile

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 2.1.A (p.3): well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM; Article 2.1.B (p.3): no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI not exceeding 6; Article 2.1.C (p.3): free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension. Article 1.5.A.1 also requires source identification including gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification before placement.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 2 applies Article 2.1.B only to the **D698/Wexford Ridge** material (68% passing No. 200, PI 11) and does not apply Articles 2.1.A/B/C to the stockpile actually placed. Action 3 asks for “gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification per Article 1.5.A.1” but does not state the Article 2.1.A/B/C acceptance criteria or require a deleterious/particle-size inspection. The deliverable never mentions the 3-inch limit, organic material, or debris; “frozen” appears only in the Article 3.3.D placement sentence (“no frozen material is recorded”), not as a material-acceptance check under Article 2.1.C. Table 1’s limits also omit the material criteria. The author’s own `requirements.csv` includes REQ-022/REQ-023/REQ-024 as applying to “All structural fill,” but the author’s `check.py` maps REQ-024 to “REF” and the DOCX does not address it.

**What it should be:** The record should require, as a condition before the fill is accepted, that the stockpile north of Block C be tested/classified against Article 2.1.A/B/C: USCS SM or SW-SM; ≤12% passing No. 200; PI ≤6; no organic material, frozen soil, debris, or particles >3 in. It should state these limits in the Basis/limits table and require the results in the action table.

**Evidence:**
- Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 p.3, Articles 2.1.A–C (quoted above).
- D1557 report p.1 describes the Larchwood Pit sample as “well-graded silty sand and gravel with occasional cobbles”; the report does not quantify the cobble size or demonstrate the 3-in limit.
- D698 report p.1–2: Wexford Ridge CL-ML, 68% passing No. 200, PI 11 — fails Article 2.1.B, but it is not the stockpile.
- Fill log Cover B23–B24: stockpile north of Block C; no gradation, Atterberg, USCS or deleterious record for that stockpile; RFI 079 retest missing.
- DOCX text search: no occurrence of “3 in”, “3 inches”, “organic”, “deleterious”, “particles”, or “debris”; “frozen” occurs once, in the Article 3.3.D weather sentence.

---

## 3. MAJOR — The 24-hour report-issue requirement of Article 3.7.B is described as “consistent” but is not demonstrated

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.7.B (p.5): “The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing.”

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 5(d): “the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated.” The action table (action 4) requires a reissued report but does not require the issue time or a 24-hour confirmation.

**What it should be:** The record should say the 24-hour requirement is **not demonstrated** from the record. The report shows only “Date Tested: 07/08/2026” and “Date Issued: 07/09/2026” (SF-26-0708 p.1); the field work ended at 11:30 on 07/08 (arrival/departure 07:15/11:30, p.1). Any issue after 11:30 on 07/09 would exceed 24 hours, and no issue time is recorded. The report should be reissued with the issue time or the Laboratory should confirm the time.

**Evidence:** SF-26-0708 p.1 dates and arrival/departure; p.2 signature date 07/09/2026; no time of issue anywhere in the report.

---

## 4. MAJOR — The calibration certificate and operator-competency records required by Article 1.4.B are not established, although the deliverable says the report satisfies the requirements “on the face”

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 1.4.B (p.2): nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation-safety training and be documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures; gauges shall be calibrated within the manufacturer’s stated interval and standard-count checked at the start of each testing day.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 5 says: “On the face of the report this satisfies the calibration and daily standard-count requirements of Spec 1.4.B (p.2).” It then lists (a) the calibration certificate was not provided and (b) no operator radiation-safety training/competence record. Action 7 requires “the gauge calibration certificate, daily standard-count record and operator radiation-safety training / D6938 competency records.”

**What it should be:** The report records standard counts (2,478 density / 738 moisture) and states that site standardization was performed on 07/08/2026, so the daily-count element is at least described; however, the calibration certificate and the operator radiation-safety/competency records are absent. The record should say those two requirements are **not verified** until the documents in action 7 are produced, not that the report satisfies the whole of Article 1.4.B on its face.

**Evidence:** SF-26-0708 p.1 §2 (gauge, serial, calibration date, standard counts, probe depth, count time, standardization statement); no calibration certificate or operator training/competency record in the corpus; DOCX Finding 5 and action 7 as quoted.

---

## 5. MINOR — The record does not establish whether Article 3.5 (backfill against walls) or Article 3.6 (settlement) applies; both are treated as not applicable without support

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.5.A/B/C (p.5): backfill against basement/foundation walls only after the wall attains 28-day strength or permanent lateral support; balanced lifts on both sides of interior walls; compact backfill to Article 3.4.B where it supports structure or slabs. Article 3.6 (p.5): total settlement 1.0 in maximum, differential 0.5 in over 30 ft, with notification before additional load.

**What the deliverable has:** No mention of Article 3.5 or 3.6. Finding 7 mentions “Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins,” “hand-compacted lifts,” and “the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls,” which shows walls are adjacent, but it applies only Article 3.4.A. The author’s `check.py` maps REQ-052–REQ-054 (Article 3.5) and REQ-055–REQ-058 (Article 3.6) to “N/A.”

**What it should be:** The record should either (a) establish that the fill is not backfill against the basement walls (and that Article 3.5 does not apply), or (b) apply Article 3.5.A/B/C and require the wall-strength/balanced-lift records. It should also state whether the Article 3.6 settlement criteria are part of the fill acceptance or are covered by a separate item; the fill is under a slab-on-grade and the record cannot simply omit the section’s settlement tolerance.

**Evidence:** Fill log Cover B29 (Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins) and Finding 7’s own “3-ft … setback from walls”; Sheet S-201 Detail 1/S-201: basement wall extends to underside of podium slab at El. 748.5; fill log finish grade El. 748.6. The DOCX contains no “3.5” article citation, no “settlement,” and no “1.0 in / 0.5 in.”

---

## 6. MINOR — The D1557 report’s own curve-fit statement does not reproduce 128.4 pcf at 9.2%; the fitted peak is about 128.2 pcf at 9.04%

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.4.B (p.4) uses the ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density and optimum moisture content.

**What the deliverable has:** 128.4 pcf maximum and 9.2% optimum, giving 121.98 pcf and 8.2%–11.2%.

**What it should be:** The Proctor report p.3 says “Curve fit: second-order polynomial through the five primary data points; peak located by first-derivative solution.” A least-squares quadratic through the five points (6.2/124.8, 7.5/127.1, 9.2/128.4, 10.8/126.7, 12.4/123.5) peaks at **128.20 pcf at 9.04%**, not 128.4/9.2; 128.4 pcf is the highest measured point. The exact 95% of the fitted peak would be 121.79 pcf and the moisture window 8.04%–11.04%. The pass/fail outcome does not change (FD-16 122.9 still passes; FD-14/FD-17 still fail), but the stated limits are not exactly the fitted peak and should be confirmed with the Laboratory.

**Evidence:** D1557 report p.2 data points; p.3 curve-fit statement and plot; independent least-squares calculation (quadratic coefficients [-0.4224, 7.6400, 93.6551], vertex at 9.0429%, 128.199 pcf).

---

## 7. MINOR — The 0.42 in of rain overnight into 07/01/2026 is omitted from the Lift 5 protection/retest discussion

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.8.A (p.6): protect completed structural fill from softening by precipitation; rework and retest any area disturbed or softened.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 7 cites only “0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift on 06/30/2026” and action 5 requires protection/retest after that event.

**What it should be:** Daily Field Report No. 144 (07/01/2026) records “0.42 in overnight (per gate gauge), trace during shift” into 07/01, after the Lift 5 placement on 06/30 and before the Lift 6 placement on 07/08. That larger event should also be included in the Lift 5 protection/retest requirement.

**Evidence:** Daily Field Reports pp.3–4, Report No. 143 (0.35 in overnight 06/30) and Report No. 144 (0.42 in overnight into 07/01).

---

## 8. MINOR — The D698 report is called the “wrong borrow” without evidence that the stockpile is not Wexford Ridge material

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1): ASTM D698 is historical borrow characterization only and not the acceptance basis; Article 2.1.B (p.3): structural fill limits.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 2 and the Documents Reviewed table call the D698/Wexford Ridge report a “different borrow source” and “wrong method and different borrow/material.”

**What it should be:** The D698 report is not the acceptance basis because it is the wrong test method and its material (CL-ML, 68% passing No. 200, PI 11) does not meet Article 2.1.B. The record does not, however, establish that the stockpile north of Block C is not Wexford Ridge Phase 1 material; the fill log does not state the stockpile’s origin, and the RFI 079 letter/retest is missing. The finding should not assert a different borrow as a fact.

**Evidence:** Fill log Cover B23 (stockpile north of Block C, no origin); D698 report p.1 (Wexford Ridge Phase 1 off-site borrow); no document tying or separating the two.

---

## 9. MINOR — The RFI 065 “one test per 500 sf” response is treated as superseded without an explicit supersession

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 3.4.B and 3.7.A.1 (pp.4–5): one test per 5,000 sf per lift and not fewer than three tests per lift.

**What the deliverable has:** Finding 4 applies 5,000 sf / three tests and says RFI 065’s “one test per 500 sf” response “conflicts with Rev.3 and is superseded by the later specification.”

**What it should be:** The current Rev.3 text supports 5,000 sf / three tests, but the record contains no explicit statement that Rev.2/Rev.3 superseded RFI 065 (answered 09/22/2025 under the earlier revision). If RFI 065 still governed, 11,400 sf would require 23 tests per lift, not 4, and the frequency conclusion would fail. The record should cite the revision history or obtain an RFI confirmation; it should not simply assert supersession.

**Evidence:** RFI Log row RFI 065 (09/22/2025); Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 revision history (Rev.2 11/14/2025 “Article 3.4 restructured”; Rev.3 03/06/2026 “Article 3.4.B acceptance criteria clarified”); no ASI/change order in the corpus.

---

## 10. MINOR — The Geotechnical Report page citation is to PDF page 20, but the report’s printed page is 19

**Requirement:** Citation accuracy; the task requires each finding to cite the document and page it rests on.

**What the deliverable has:** “Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), page 20” (Finding 1; Documents Reviewed table “Page 20”).

**What it should be:** The 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% text is on PDF page 20 of the 21-page file, but the report’s own footer on that page is “Page 19.” The citation should say “PDF p.20 / report p.19” or similar.

**Evidence:** Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, PDF page marker `--- page 20 ---`, footer “Page 19”; text at lines 878–882.

---

## 11. MINOR — The action for failing tests does not state that rework is at the Contractor’s expense

**Requirement:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.4.C.1 (p.5): the affected area shall be reworked “at the Contractor’s expense.”

**What the deliverable has:** Action 1: “Rework and retest Lift 6 at FD-14 … and FD-17 …” with owner “Rowan Bay / Vantree”; no expense statement.

**What it should be:** Add “at the Contractor’s expense” to action 1, consistent with Article 3.4.C.1.

**Evidence:** Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 p.5 Article 3.4.C.1; DOCX action table row 1.

---

## 12. MINOR — The “limits it produces” table omits the material, hold-point and protection limits that the findings rely on

**Requirement:** Task instruction: “State the acceptance basis you are using, the limits it produces, and what in the record establishes that basis for this fill.” Spec 31 20 00 Articles 2.1.A/B/C, 1.6.A/B, 3.3.A/B/D, 3.4.A, 3.8.A.

**What the deliverable has:** Table 1 lists reference standard, dry density, moisture, both criteria, frequency, lift thickness, reporting and nonconforming work. It does not list the Article 2.1.A/B/C material limits, the Article 1.6.A/B proof-roll/prior-lift hold points, the Article 3.4.A hand-lift/setback limits, or the Article 3.8.A protection requirement, although some appear in Findings 5/7 and the action table.

**What it should be:** Add these limits to Table 1 or cross-reference the findings so the reader can see the complete set of acceptance limits in one place.

**Evidence:** DOCX Table 1; Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 pp.2–6; DOCX Findings 5 and 7 and actions 6/8.

---

## 13. MINOR — The register status is ambiguous: “review is closed” while the fill remains unaccepted

[P22] Each finding cites the document and page it rests on. The recomputation of the four tests is set out in Table 1 at Finding 3.
[P23] Finding 1 — The governing acceptance standard is ASTM D1557 Method C, not ASTM D698. Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill; Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) sets the 95% density and −1%/+2% moisture criteria against that D1557 result. Verification Register Item 027 (closed 03/13/2026) confirms both criteria bind independently. Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), page 20, states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. [P25] Finding 3 — Re-evaluated against the D1557 Method C values, density passes at all four locations, but moisture fails at FD-14 and FD-17. Table 1 recomputes each result. The correct percent compaction is dry density ÷ 128.4 × 100; the correct moisture deviation is measured moisture minus 9.2%.
[P26] Table 1 — Tests FD-14 through FD-17 recomputed against ASTM D1557 Method C (128.4 pcf, 9.2%). Inputs from SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; D1557 values from VMT-25-0918-P04 p.3.

FD-15 | Grid D-5 | 748.6 | 6 | 123.5 | 9.8 | 96.2 | PASS | +0.6 | PASS | PASS
FD-16 | Grid F-4 | 748.6 | 6 | 122.9 | 10.4 | 95.7 | PASS | +1.2 | PASS | PASS
FD-17 | Grid G-2 | 748.6 | 6 | 126.1 | 5.8 | 98.2 | PASS | −3.4 | FAIL | FAIL
[/TABLE]
[P28] FD-14 is 6.1% moisture, 3.1 percentage points below optimum and 2.1 points below the 8.2% lower limit. FD-17 is 5.8%, 3.4 points below optimum and 2.4 points below the lower limit. FD-15 (9.8%) and FD-16 (10.4%) are within 8.2% to 11.2% and pass both criteria. The density margin at FD-16 is thin: 122.9 pcf is 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point) above the 121.98 pcf minimum. Under Spec 3.4.B and 3.4.D (pp.4–5), both criteria must be satisfied at each location; under 3.4.C.3 (p.5), failing results may not be averaged with passing results. Lift 6 therefore fails acceptance as tested.
[P29] Finding 4 — The number and distribution of Lift 6 tests satisfy the frequency requirement, but the record covers only Lift 6. The pad area is 11,400 sf (Fill Log Cover B22; Notes 1; Daily Log row 24). At one test per 5,000 sf, 11,400/5,000 = 2.28, so three tests per lift are required; Article 3.7.A.1 also sets a floor of three tests per lift. Four tests were taken — FD-14 at Grid B-3, FD-15 at Grid D-5, FD-16 at Grid F-4 and FD-17 at Grid G-2 — all at El. 748.6 in Lift 6 (SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; Fill Log Daily Log row 24). The frequency requirement is met with one test to spare. The log shows six lifts from El. 745.0 to El. 748.6, 3.6 ft total, at 8 in loose / 7.2 in compacted per lift (Cover B18–B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the 8 in Lift 6 thickness is within the 12 in limit. Lift 6 was placed in clear weather at 71–84 °F with no precipitation (Daily Log row 24), and no frozen material is recorded, consistent with Article 3.3.D. RFI 065 (response 09/22/2025) states one test per 500 sf; that earlier response conflicts with Rev.3 and is superseded by the later specification. I applied Rev.3’s 5,000 sf / minimum three per lift. The other five lifts are outside SF-26-0708 and are addressed in Finding 7.
[P30] Finding 5 — The testing was performed by the Owner’s independent laboratory with a calibrated gauge, but the report and record have gaps that prevent it from being a complete acceptance document. The report is sealed by Talia Brennard, PE (p.2), and is authentic as a Vantree document; the deficiencies are technical. The D1557 report states that the Laboratory is contracted to the Owner (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 3), consistent with Spec 1.4.A. SF-26-0708 shows Vantree as the testing laboratory, Thornbury State University as client, a Troxler Model 3440 gauge (serial 34-047162), calibration dated 02/06/2026, standard counts of 2,478 density / 738 moisture, site standardization on 07/08/2026 before the first test, 60-second counts and ASTM D6938 direct transmission (p.1). On the face of the report this satisfies the calibration and daily standard-count requirements of Spec 1.4.B (p.2). However: (a) the calibration certificate is only “on file” and was not provided; (b) there is no record of the operator’s current radiation-safety training or documented competence in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures, required by 1.4.B; (c) the probe depth is 6 in while the compacted lift is 7.2 in (Fill Log Cover B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the bottom 1.2 in of the lift was not sampled and full-thickness compliance under 3.3.C is not demonstrated; (d) the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated; and (e) as found in Finding 2, it reports density only and against the wrong D698 reference. These are record deficiencies, not merely presentation issues.
[P31] Finding 6 — The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed, and the FD-16 density margin is too thin to absorb a different Proctor. The fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse under RFI 079 (Fill Log Cover B23; Notes 4). It carries VMT-25-0918-P04, the Larchwood Pit D1557, as the governing Proctor (Cover B24; Notes 5). The only D1557 report in the record is for Larchwood Pit (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1) and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (p.4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record, and there is no D1557 on the stockpile material. Spec 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 values to be those of the material actually placed, and 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially. The record therefore does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the correct denominator for the stockpile. That matters: FD-16 passes by only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point), so a material-specific maximum dry density higher than about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. The D1557 values used in Finding 3 are the correct method and the only D1557 on file, but they are not a substitute for the stockpile-specific determination.
[P32] Finding 7 — The record does not demonstrate that Lifts 1 through 5 were accepted, or that the subgrade and test-strip hold points were closed with test evidence. The fill log states that Lifts 1 through 5 are covered by FDR-BA-01 through FDR-BA-05, three tests per lift (Cover B31; Notes 6), and that each lift was tested before the next was placed (Notes 6; Daily Log rows 19–23). Those five reports are not in the review record, so their density/moisture results and dispositions cannot be checked. The log also records a rework of about 1,500 sf near Grid E-4 in Lift 5 for moisture correction (Daily Log row 23); no retest result for that rework is in the record. Daily Field Report No. 143 (06/30/2026) records 0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift; the package contains no Lift 5 protection or post-rain retest record for that surface. The subgrade proof-roll is recorded only as a log statement — loaded tandem-axle dump truck, Vantree present, 06/18/2026 — with written acceptance said to be memo TPM-26-063 dated 06/18/2026 (Cover B26; Notes 2); the log does not record the 20-ton loaded tandem required by RFI 118 (response 03/09/2026), and the memo is not attached. The test strip is recorded as executed 06/19/2026, witnessed by Vantree and Thelbridge, with six passes (Cover B27; Notes 3), but no test-strip results demonstrating Article 3.4.B compliance are in the record. For Lift 6 itself, the log records six smooth-drum passes and four pneumatic/plate passes (Daily Log row 24), matching the six-pass test-strip pattern; the procedure appears to have been followed, but procedure alone does not cure the moisture failures. The log also records the Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins but not the loose thickness of those hand-compacted lifts or the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls; Article 3.4.A requires those hand lifts to be not more than 6 in and prohibits heavy equipment within 3 ft of walls before balanced backfill. Spec 1.6.A/B (p.3) and 3.4.A/C (pp.4–5) make these hold points and prior-lift acceptances prerequisites. They must be produced before the fill as a whole can be accepted, even if Lift 6 is later reworked and retested.
[P33] Finding 8 — The open moisture RFI does not change the criteria. RFI 125, raised 07/08/2026, asks for an interpretation of the moisture criteria on SF-26-0708; the RFI log shows no response and status Open (RFI Log row RFI 125). No waiver, variance or revision to Spec 31 20 00 is in the record. The criteria of Article 3.4.B apply as written. If the Contractor disputes the nuclear moisture values, ASTM D2216 is the referee method under Article 1.2.A.4; a referee result would still be evaluated against the same 8.2% to 11.2% window. RFI 065’s earlier “one test per 500 sf” response is likewise not a basis to alter the later Rev.3 frequency; Rev.3 governs.
[P34] Finding 9 — The Contractor’s 07/14/2026 pour-readiness statement is a density-only claim against the wrong reference; it is not acceptance evidence. The

PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content
