--- page 2 ---
when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 3 ---
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 5 ---
3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

A.   Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.
Rework and retest, at the Contractor's expense, any area disturbed or softened prior to
permanent cover.

The plant-room excavation is planned to reach subgrade at approximately El. 726.0, which lies within the CL
clay approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined SW-GW aquifer at El. 720.0. The confined piezometric
head in the aquifer is at El. 738.0 (Section 7.2), i.e., approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade.
This excavation will develop confined-aquifer uplift on the clay plug that separates the subgrade from the
aquifer (Section 8.2). The clay-plug residual thickness of only 6 ft is not, on its own, sufficient to resist the
uplift pressure with an adequate factor of safety against
. Design mitigation is required. Options that
the design team should evaluate include, individually or in combination:
•  Pressure-relief wells screened in the aquifer at or immediately outside the excavation footprint, pumped
to reduce the piezometric head at the excavation subgrade elevation to a value that provides an adequate

9.5  Engineered Fill Placement over the Clay
Bringing the Block B footprint to design grade requires placement of engineered fill of nominal 12 ft thickness
(from natural ground at El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0). Because there is no substantial engineered fill
or naturally overconsolidated material above the clay at Block B, the engineered fill is placed directly on the
stripped clay surface after topsoil removal only.
The engineered fill loads the underlying normally-consolidated CL clay as an areal surcharge, and consolidation
of the clay under the fill surcharge will occur. Under the parameters of Table 5-1, the settlement caused by 12 ft
of fill placed as a wide, essentially areal surcharge is substantial and will accrue over a period on the order of
years. The engineering consequences must be reconciled by the design team:
•  If the fill is placed and given time to allow the underlying clay to substantially complete primary
consolidation before piles are driven and the podium is erected, then the residual downdrag on the piles
(and the residual differential settlement of any structure bearing at grade) is minimized. This is the
preferred sequence.

9.6  Dewatering, Excavation and Construction Considerations
•  The basement excavation for Blocks A and B, with a subgrade at approximately El. 731.5, is above the
top of the clay (El. 738.0) and above the confined head (El. 738.0), but it is below the shallow water table
(El. 742.0). Dewatering to control the shallow water table will be required in the upper sand around the
basement excavation but will not reduce the confined head in the deep aquifer, and is not by itself a
mitigation for the plant-room base-heave problem.
•  The confined-aquifer condition and the aquitard behavior of the CL clay must be preserved. Any activity
that penetrates the clay across the plant-room footprint — including piles, pressure-relief wells, or shoring
elements — must be sealed at the aquitard elevation so as not to short-circuit the aquitard.
•  Temporary sheeting design is a delegated design and is not scoped in this report; however, the shoring
designer must be furnished with the confined head El. 738.0, the shallow water table El. 742.0, and the
strength parameters and unit weights of each stratum for use in the shoring calculations.
•  Dewatering discharge is subject to Ohio EPA NPDES permitting requirements.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.

def set_run(run, size=10, bold=False, italic=False, color=None):
    run.font.name='Calibri'
    run._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:cs'),'Calibri')
    run._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:eastAsia'),'Calibri')
    run._element.rPr.rFonts.set(qn('w:hAnsi'),'Calibri')
    run.font.size=Pt(size)
    run.bold=bold
    run.italic=italic
    if color:
        run.font.color.rgb=RGBColor(*color)

def clear_para(p):
    for r in list(p.runs):
        r._element.getparent().remove(r._element)
    # remove hyperlinks / other content except pPr
    for child in list(p._p):
        if child.tag != qn('w:pPr'):
            p._p.remove(child)

def fmt_para(p, before=0, after=3, line=1.0, left=0, hanging=None, align=None, keep_next=False):
    pf=p.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before=Pt(before)
    pf.space_after=Pt(after)
    pf.line_spacing=line
    if left:
        pf.left_indent=Inches(left)
    if hanging:
        pf.first_line_indent=Inches(-hanging)
    if align is not None:
        p.alignment=align
    if keep_next:
        pf.keep_with_next=True

def content_para(anchor, text='', bold=False, italic=False, size=10, before=0, after=3, left=0, hanging=None, align=None, color=None):
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    if text:
        r=p.add_run(text)
        set_run(r,size=size,bold=bold,italic=italic,color=color)
    fmt_para(p,before=before,after=after,left=left,hanging=hanging,align=align)
    return p

def rich_para(anchor, parts, size=10, before=0, after=3, left=0, hanging=None):
    """parts = list of (text,bold,italic) tuples."""
    p=doc.add_paragraph()
    anchor._p.addnext(p._p)
    for text,bold,italic in parts:
        r=p.add_run(text)
        set_run(r,size=size,bold=bold,italic=italic)
    fmt_para(p,before=before,after=after,left=left,hanging=hanging)
    return p

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd=OxmlElement('w:shd')
    shd.set(qn('w:val'),'clear')
    shd.set(qn('w:color'),'auto')
    shd.set(qn('w:fill'),hexcolor)
    tcPr.append(shd)

def set_cell_margins(cell, top=40, bottom=40, left=60, right=60):
    tcPr=cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    tcMar=OxmlElement('w:tcMar')
    for tag,val in [('top',top),('bottom',bottom),('left',left),('right',right)]:
        node=OxmlElement(f'w:{tag}')
        node.set(qn('w:w'),str(val)); node.set(qn('w:type'),'dxa')
        tcMar.append(node)
    tcPr.append(tcMar)

def add_table(anchor, headers, rows, widths, font_size=8.5, header_fill='D9E2F3'):
    t=doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers))
    t.alignment=WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit=False
    # manual single-line borders (template has no Table Grid style)
    tblPr=t._tbl.tblPr
    borders=OxmlElement('w:tblBorders')
    for edge in ('top','left','bottom','right','insideH','insideV'):
        el=OxmlElement(f'w:{edge}')
        el.set(qn('w:val'),'single'); el.set(qn('w:sz'),'4'); el.set(qn('w:space'),'0'); el.set(qn('w:color'),'808080')
        borders.append(el)
    tblPr.append(borders)
    # move after anchor
    anchor._p.addnext(t._tbl)
    # header
    hdr=t.rows[0].cells
    for j,h in enumerate(headers):
        hdr[j].text=''
        p=hdr[j].paragraphs[0]
        r=p.add_run(h); set_run(r,size=font_size,bold=True)
        fmt_para(p,after=0,line=1.0)
        shade(hdr[j],header_fill)
        set_cell_margins(hdr[j])
    # body
    for row in rows:
        cells=t.add_row().cells
        for j,val in enumerate(row):
            cells[j].text=''
            p=cells[j].paragraphs[0]
            r=p.add_run(str(val)); set_run(r,size=font_size)
            fmt_para(p,after=0,line=1.0)
            set_cell_margins(cells[j])
    # widths
    for j,w in enumerate(widths):
        t.columns[j].width=Inches(w)
        for cell in t.columns[j].cells:
            cell.width=Inches(w)
    # repeat header row and keep rows from splitting across pages
    for row in t.rows:
        trPr=row._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
        cantSplit=OxmlElement('w:cantSplit'); cantSplit.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(cantSplit)
    trPr=t.rows[0]._tr.get_or_add_trPr()
    tblHeader=OxmlElement('w:tblHeader'); tblHeader.set(qn('w:val'),'true'); trPr.append(tblHeader)
    # spacer after table
    sp=doc.add_paragraph()
    t._tbl.addnext(sp._p)
    fmt_para(sp,after=2,line=1.0)
    return sp

Four tests were taken — FD-14 at Grid B-3, FD-15 at Grid D-5, FD-16 at Grid F-4 and FD-17 at Grid G-2 — all at El. 748.6 in Lift 6 (SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; Fill Log Daily Log row 24). The frequency requirement is met with one test to spare. The log shows six lifts from El. 745.0 to El. 748.6, 3.6 ft total, at 8 in loose / 7.2 in compacted per lift (Cover B18–B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the 8 in Lift 6 thickness is within the 12 in limit. Lift 6 was placed in clear weather at 71–84 °F with no precipitation (Daily Log row 24), and no frozen material is recorded, consistent with Article 3.3.D. RFI 065 (response 09/22/2025) states one test per 500 sf; that earlier response conflicts with Rev.3 and is superseded by the later specification. I applied Rev.3’s 5,000 sf / minimum three per lift. The other five lifts are outside SF-26-0708 and are addressed in Finding 7.')

cur=finding(cur,'Finding 5 — The testing was performed by the Owner’s independent laboratory with a calibrated gauge, but the report and record have gaps that prevent it from being a complete acceptance document.',
 'The report is sealed by Talia Brennard, PE (p.2), and is authentic as a Vantree document; the deficiencies are technical. The D1557 report states that the Laboratory is contracted to the Owner (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 3), consistent with Spec 1.4.A. SF-26-0708 shows Vantree as the testing laboratory, Thornbury State University as client, a Troxler Model 3440 gauge (serial 34-047162), calibration dated 02/06/2026, standard counts of 2,478 density / 738 moisture, site standardization on 07/08/2026 before the first test, 60-second counts and ASTM D6938 direct transmission (p.1). On the face of the report this satisfies the calibration and daily standard-count requirements of Spec 1.4.B (p.2). However: (a) the calibration certificate is only “on file” and was not provided; (b) there is no record of the operator’s current radiation-safety training or documented competence in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures, required by 1.4.B; (c) the probe depth is 6 in while the compacted lift is 7.2 in (Fill Log Cover B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the bottom 1.2 in of the lift was not sampled and full-thickness compliance under 3.3.C is not demonstrated; (d) the report was issued the day after testing, consistent with the 24-hour requirement on the dates shown, but the issue time is not stated; and (e) as found in Finding 2, it reports density only and against the wrong D698 reference. These are record deficiencies, not merely presentation issues.')

cur=finding(cur,'Finding 6 — The D1557 denominator is not tied to the stockpile actually placed, and the FD-16 density margin is too thin to absorb a different Proctor.',
 'The fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse under RFI 079 (Fill Log Cover B23; Notes 4). It carries VMT-25-0918-P04, the Larchwood Pit D1557, as the governing Proctor (Cover B24; Notes 5). The only D1557 report in the record is for Larchwood Pit (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1) and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (p.4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record, and there is no D1557 on the stockpile material. Spec 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 values to be those of the material actually placed, and 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially. The record therefore does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the correct denominator for the stockpile. That matters: FD-16 passes by only 0.9 pcf (0.7 percentage point), so a material-specific maximum dry density higher than about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. The D1557 values used in Finding 3 are the correct method and the only D1557 on file, but they are not a substitute for the stockpile-specific determination.')

cur=finding(cur,'Finding 7 — The record does not demonstrate that Lifts 1 through 5 were accepted, or that the subgrade and test-strip hold points were closed with test evidence.',
 'The fill log states that Lifts 1 through 5 are covered by FDR-BA-01 through FDR-BA-05, three tests per lift (Cover B31; Notes 6), and that each lift was tested before the next was placed (Notes 6; Daily Log rows 19–23). Those five reports are not in the review record, so their density/moisture results and dispositions cannot be checked. The log also records a rework of about 1,500 sf near Grid E-4 in Lift 5 for moisture correction (Daily Log row 23); no retest result for that rework is in the record. Daily Field Report No. 143 (06/30/2026) records 0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift; the package contains no Lift 5 protection or post-rain retest record for that surface. The subgrade proof-roll is recorded only as a log statement — loaded tandem-axle dump truck, Vantree present, 06/18/2026 — with written acceptance said to be memo TPM-26-063 dated 06/18/2026 (Cover B26; Notes 2); the log does not record the 20-ton loaded tandem required by RFI 118 (response 03/09/2026), and the memo is not attached. The test strip is recorded as executed 06/19/2026, witnessed by Vantree and Thelbridge, with six passes (Cover B27; Notes 3), but no test-strip results demonstrating Article 3.4.B compliance are in the record. For Lift 6 itself, the log records six smooth-drum passes and four pneumatic/plate passes (Daily Log row 24), matching the six-pass test-strip pattern; the procedure appears to have been followed, but procedure alone does not cure the moisture failures. The log also records the Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins but not the loose thickness of those hand-compacted lifts or the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback from walls; Article 3.4.A requires those hand lifts to be not more than 6 in and prohibits heavy equipment within 3 ft of walls before balanced backfill. Spec 1.6.A/B (p.3) and 3.4.A/C (pp.4–5) make these hold points and prior-lift acceptances prerequisites. They must be produced before the fill as a whole can be accepted, even if Lift 6 is later reworked and retested.')

cur=finding(cur,'Finding 8 — The open moisture RFI does not change the criteria.',
 'RFI 125, raised 07/08/2026, asks for an interpretation of the moisture criteria on SF-26-0708; the RFI log shows no response and status Open (RFI Log row RFI 125). No waiver, variance or revision to Spec 31 20 00 is in the record. The criteria of Article 3.4.B apply as written. If the Contractor disputes the nuclear moisture values, ASTM D2216 is the referee method under Article 1.2.A.4; a referee result would still be evaluated against the same 8.2% to 11.2% window. RFI 065’s earlier “one test per 500 sf” response is likewise not a basis to alter the later Rev.3 frequency; Rev.3 governs.')

cur=finding(cur,'Finding 9 — The Contractor’s 07/14/2026 pour-readiness statement is a density-only claim against the wrong reference; it is not acceptance evidence.',
 'The notification states that “all four tests exceed 95% requirement” (S. Kendrow email, 07/14/2026, item (b)). That statement refers only to density and is computed against the wrong D698 reference; it does not address the moisture failures at FD-14 and FD-17. It is a Contractor assertion, not test evidence, and cannot support acceptance.')

# ------------- 5. CONCLUSION -------------
p_concl=find_para('5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION')
p_concl_ph=find_para('State the determination using ACCEPTED or REJECTED')
clear_para(p_concl_ph)
r=p_concl_ph.add_run('Determination: REJECTED. This record closes the Item 054 review with a determination of REJECTED; the fill itself is not accepted. Lift 6 does not meet Specification Section 31 20 00 Article 3.4.B: FD-14 and FD-17 fail the moisture criterion, and the report’s D698/Wexford Ridge reference is not the governing basis. The passing density results at FD-15 and FD-16 do not cure the failures because acceptance is evaluated at each test location and the criteria are independent (Articles 3.4.C.3 and 3.4.D). Item 054 must not be recorded as ACCEPTED.')
set_run(r,size=10); fmt_para(p_concl_ph,after=4)
cur=p_concl_ph
cur=content_para(cur,'Before the capillary break, slab-on-grade, MEP, or any other permanent work is placed on this fill, the following must be in hand and accepted by Thelbridge:',after=3)
cur.paragraph_format.page_break_before=True
actions=[
 ('1','Rework and retest Lift 6 at FD-14 (Grid B-3) and FD-17 (Grid G-2), and any additional area shown by the Contractor’s moisture survey to be drier than 8.2%. Moisture-condition and recompact; retest both density and moisture at the same locations; do not average failing results with passing results.','Rowan Bay / Vantree','Sealed retest report showing both criteria pass at each location'),
 ('2','Define and document the affected area and rework extents, including a sketch of the rework limits and retest locations.','Rowan Bay','Rework plan and location sketch'),
 ('3','Obtain ASTM D1557 Method C on the stockpile north of Block C; provide the reviewed placement and compaction plan (Article 1.5.A.3), gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification per Article 1.5.A.1, and the RFI 079 gradation retest / letter TPM-25-079. If the stockpile Proctor differs from 128.4 pcf / 9.2%, re-evaluate all tests against the correct values.','Rowan Bay / Vantree','Sealed D1557 report, placement plan, and source data for the stockpile'),
 ('4','Reissue SF-26-0708 as Rev.1 or a supplemental report using the correct D1557 denominators, recomputed percent compaction, moisture deviation, and a per-location accept/reject disposition for both criteria, including all retests.','Vantree','Sealed revised/supplemental field density report'),
 ('5','Provide FDR-BA-01 through FDR-BA-05 for Lifts 1 through 5, including the Lift 5 rework retest, and confirm that the Lift 5 surface was protected and retested as necessary after the 0.35 in overnight rain recorded on 06/30/2026; show both criteria against the correct D1557 values.','Rowan Bay / Vantree','Complete lift reports, post-rain protection/retest record, and acceptance record'),

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent recomputation for Item 054 — Block A slab-on-grade fill compaction.
All inputs are taken from the project record; no value is adopted from the deliverable.
"""
from math import ceil
import csv, json, os

# ---------- Inputs from the record ----------
# Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, 03/06/2026, Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 3.4.B, 3.4.C, 3.7.A.1
D1557_REQUIRED_PCT = 95.0          # % of D1557 max dry density
MOISTURE_LOWER = -1.0              # % of optimum
MOISTURE_UPPER = 2.0               # % of optimum
MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT = 3             # Article 3.7.A.1
TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF = 5000.0     # Article 3.4.B / 3.7.A.1
MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN = 12.0           # Article 3.3.A
HAND_LIFT_IN = 6.0                 # Article 3.4.A
REPORT_HOURS = 24.0                # Article 3.7.B

# Vantree Report VMT-25-0918-P04, 09/18/2025, ASTM D1557-12(2021) Method C, Larchwood Pit
GAMMA_D_MAX = 128.4                # pcf
W_OPT = 9.2                        # %
# Vantree Report VMT-2024-0403-P1B, 04/03/2024, ASTM D698 Method A, Wexford Ridge (NOT acceptance basis)
GAMMA_D_MAX_D698 = 118.6           # pcf
W_OPT_D698 = 12.1                  # %

# Fill Placement and Grading Records — Block A Slab-on-Grade, RB-FPR-BA-2026
PAD_AREA_SF = 11400.0
LIFTS = [
    # lift, date, top El. ft, loose in, compacted in, area sf, tests taken, report
    (1, '06/22/2026', 745.6, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-01'),
    (2, '06/23/2026', 746.2, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-02'),
    (3, '06/25/2026', 746.8, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-03'),
    (4, '06/26/2026', 747.4, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-04'),
    (5, '06/30/2026', 748.0, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 3, 'FDR-BA-05'),
    (6, '07/08/2026', 748.6, 8.0, 7.2, 11400.0, 4, 'SF-26-0708'),
]
# Field Density Report SF-26-0708, page 1-2, tests FD-14..FD-17
TESTS = [
    # id, elev ft, location, lift, dry density pcf, moisture %, reported % vs D698, reported disposition
    ('FD-14', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid B-3', 6, 124.8, 6.1, 105.2, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-15', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid D-5', 6, 123.5, 9.8, 104.1, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-16', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid F-4', 6, 122.9, 10.4, 103.6, 'PASS'),
    ('FD-17', 748.6, 'Block A, Grid G-2', 6, 126.1, 5.8, 106.3, 'PASS'),
]
PROBE_DEPTH_IN = 6.0
REPORT_TEST_DATE = '07/08/2026'
REPORT_ISSUE_DATE = '07/09/2026'

# ---------- Derived limits ----------
REQ_DENSITY = GAMMA_D_MAX * D1557_REQUIRED_PCT / 100.0          # 121.98 pcf
MOIST_LOW = W_OPT + MOISTURE_LOWER                              # 8.2 %
MOIST_HIGH = W_OPT + MOISTURE_UPPER                             # 11.2 %
D1557_95_ROUNDED = 122.0                                        # value printed in VMT-25-0918-P04

print('ITEM 054 — INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION')
print('='*78)
print(f'D1557 Method C: gamma_d,max = {GAMMA_D_MAX:.1f} pcf, w_opt = {W_OPT:.1f} %')
print(f'Required density = {D1557_REQUIRED_PCT:.0f}% x {GAMMA_D_MAX:.1f} = {REQ_DENSITY:.2f} pcf (report rounds {D1557_95_ROUNDED:.1f} pcf)')
print(f'Acceptable moisture = {W_OPT:.1f} {MOISTURE_LOWER:+.0f}% to {W_OPT:.1f} {MOISTURE_UPPER:+.0f}% = {MOIST_LOW:.1f}% to {MOIST_HIGH:.1f}%')
print(f'D698 (not acceptance basis): gamma_d,max = {GAMMA_D_MAX_D698:.1f} pcf, w_opt = {W_OPT_D698:.1f} %')
print()

# ---------- Test-by-test recomputation ----------
print('TEST RESULTS RECOMPUTED AGAINST D1557 METHOD C')
print('-'*78)
print(f"{'Test':<6}{'DD pcf':>8}{'w %':>7}{'%comp':>8}{'density':>10}{'dw':>7}{'moisture':>10}{'overall':>10}")
results = []
for tid, elev, loc, lift, dd, w, rep_pct, rep_disp in TESTS:
    pct = dd / GAMMA_D_MAX * 100.0
    dw = w - W_OPT
    density_ok = pct >= D1557_REQUIRED_PCT
    moisture_ok = MOIST_LOW <= w <= MOIST_HIGH
    overall = 'PASS' if (density_ok and moisture_ok) else 'FAIL'
    results.append(dict(id=tid, elev=elev, loc=loc, lift=lift, dd=dd, w=w, pct=pct, dw=dw,
                        density_ok=density_ok, moisture_ok=moisture_ok, overall=overall,
                        rep_pct=rep_pct, rep_disp=rep_disp))
    print(f'{tid:<6}{dd:>8.1f}{w:>7.1f}{pct:>8.1f}{("PASS" if density_ok else "FAIL"):>10}{dw:>+7.1f}{("PASS" if moisture_ok else "FAIL"):>10}{overall:>10}')
print()
for r in results:
    check_d698 = r['dd'] / GAMMA_D_MAX_D698 * 100.0
    print(f"{r['id']}: reported {r['rep_pct']:.1f}% vs D698 {GAMMA_D_MAX_D698:.1f} pcf (recomputed {check_d698:.1f}%); "
          f"correct D1557 %comp {r['pct']:.2f}%; moisture {r['w']:.1f}% vs {MOIST_LOW:.1f}-{MOIST_HIGH:.1f}%")
print()

# ---------- Worst-case utilisation per hard limit ----------
print('WORST-CASE UTILISATION PER HARD LIMIT (<=1.0 passes)')
print('-'*78)
# density: required / actual
density_utils = [(REQ_DENSITY / r['dd'], r['id'], r['dd']) for r in results]
worst_density = max(density_utils)
print(f'Density: worst {worst_density[1]} actual {worst_density[2]:.1f} pcf, required {REQ_DENSITY:.2f} pcf -> utilisation {worst_density[0]:.4f}')
# moisture: exceedance / allowed excursion on the side exceeded (or 0 if inside)
moist_utils = []
for r in results:
    if r['w'] < MOIST_LOW:
        u = (MOIST_LOW - r['w']) / abs(MOISTURE_LOWER)
    elif r['w'] > MOIST_HIGH:
        u = (r['w'] - MOIST_HIGH) / abs(MOISTURE_UPPER)
    else:
        u = 0.0
    moist_utils.append((u, r['id'], r['w']))
worst_moist = max(moist_utils)
print(f'Moisture: worst {worst_moist[1]} actual {worst_moist[2]:.1f}%, window {MOIST_LOW:.1f}-{MOIST_HIGH:.1f}% -> utilisation {worst_moist[0]:.4f}')
# frequency, every lift
freq_rows = []
for lift, date, elev, loose, comp, area, tests, report in LIFTS:
    required = max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(area / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF))
    freq_rows.append((required / tests, lift, required, tests, report))
worst_freq = max(freq_rows)
print(f'Frequency: worst Lift {worst_freq[1]} required {worst_freq[2]} tests, provided {worst_freq[3]} -> utilisation {worst_freq[0]:.4f}')
# lift thickness, every lift
thick_rows = [(loose / MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN, lift, loose) for lift, date, elev, loose, comp, area, tests, report in LIFTS]
worst_thick = max(thick_rows)
print(f'Loose lift thickness: worst Lift {worst_thick[1]} {worst_thick[2]:.1f} in / {MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN:.0f} in -> utilisation {worst_thick[0]:.4f}')
# probe depth vs compacted thickness (full-thickness coverage indicator)
probe_cov = PROBE_DEPTH_IN / LIFTS[-1][4]
print(f'Probe depth: {PROBE_DEPTH_IN:.1f} in in a {LIFTS[-1][4]:.1f} in compacted lift -> sampled fraction {probe_cov:.3f} (bottom {LIFTS[-1][4]-PROBE_DEPTH_IN:.1f} in not sampled)')
# report timing
print(f'Report timing: tested {REPORT_TEST_DATE}, issued {REPORT_ISSUE_DATE} -> 1 day vs {REPORT_HOURS:.0f} h limit (exact hours not stated)')
# total thickness / elevation
total_in = sum(l[4] for l in LIFTS)
print(f'Lift geometry: {len(LIFTS)} lifts x {LIFTS[0][4]:.1f} in compacted = {total_in:.1f} in = {total_in/12:.2f} ft; 745.0 + {total_in/12:.2f} = {745.0+total_in/12:.1f} ft')
print()

# ---------- Acceptance conclusion ----------
failed = [r['id'] for r in results if r['overall'] == 'FAIL']
print('CONCLUSION')
print('-'*78)
print(f'Tests meeting both criteria: {[r["id"] for r in results if r["overall"]=="PASS"]}')
print(f'Tests failing one or more criteria: {failed}')
print(f'Overall Lift 6 determination: {"ACCEPTED" if not failed else "REJECTED"}')
print(f'Density passes all four; moisture fails FD-14 (dry by {MOIST_LOW-TESTS[0][5]:.1f} points) and FD-17 (dry by {MOIST_LOW-TESTS[3][5]:.1f} points).')
print()

# ---------- Check the requirement table values that are directly computable ----------
print('REQUIREMENT-TABLE CHECK (numeric limits directly applicable to Item 054)')
print('-'*78)
req_checks = {
    'REQ-041': (min(r['pct'] for r in results) >= D1557_REQUIRED_PCT, f'minimum %comp {min(r["pct"] for r in results):.2f} >= 95'),
    'REQ-042': (all(MOIST_LOW <= r['w'] <= MOIST_HIGH for r in results), f'moisture values {[r["w"] for r in results]} in {MOIST_LOW}-{MOIST_HIGH}'),
    'REQ-043': (all(r['density_ok'] and r['moisture_ok'] for r in results), 'both criteria at every test location'),
    'REQ-044': (all(t >= max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(a / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF)) for _,_,_,_,_,a,t,_ in LIFTS), 'frequency per lift'),
    'REQ-059': (all(t >= max(MIN_TESTS_PER_LIFT, ceil(a / TEST_AREA_PER_TEST_SF)) for _,_,_,_,_,a,t,_ in LIFTS), 'frequency and minimum three per lift'),
    'REQ-031': (all(l[3] <= MAX_LOOSE_LIFT_IN for l in LIFTS), 'loose lift <=12 in'),
    'REQ-047': (all(r['overall'] == 'PASS' for r in results), 'retest not available; original failing locations not both passing'),
}
for rid,(ok,desc) in req_checks.items():
    print(f'{rid}: {"PASS" if ok else "FAIL"} — {desc}')
print()
print('Non-numeric/record checks (addressed in the acceptance record):')
print('- REQ-003/004: D698 not acceptance basis; D1557 governs — report uses D698, so reporting basis is nonconforming.')
print('- REQ-014/015: D1557 on material actually placed at each location — only Larchwood Pit D1557 on file; stockpile north of Block C not tested.')
print('- REQ-019/062: report must give D1557 denominators, moisture deviation and dual disposition — SF-26-0708 does not.')
print('- REQ-020/071: written subgrade proof-roll acceptance — memo TPM-26-063 cited but not in review record.')
print('- REQ-037: test strip must demonstrate criteria — log records test strip but no test results on file.')
print('- REQ-061: report within 24 h — next-day issue meets date evidence but issue time is not stated.')
print('- REQ-012/013: operator training and gauge calibration — calibration date and standard counts stated; certificate/competency records not in record.')

# Write machine-readable results
os.makedirs('/tmp/ahpele/out', exist_ok=True)
json.dump(dict(limits=dict(req_density=REQ_DENSITY,moist_low=MOIST_LOW,moist_high=MOIST_HIGH,
                          gamma_d_max=GAMMA_D_MAX,w_opt=W_OPT),
               results=results, failed=failed, freq=freq_rows, lifts=LIFTS),
          open('/tmp/ahpele/out/verify_results.json','w'), indent=2)

With the Level-3 concrete placement on 07/22/2026 approaching and several items still open on the Package A register, I want to confirm the position we agreed at award: no permanent work on Package A proceeds until Thelbridge has issued a written verification. That is the hold-point we set at Notice to Proceed, and it applies equally to the Level-3 pour and to every other operation on the current list.

Please close the current list — the shoring for the August Block B excavation, the pile downdrag question, the mat buoyancy check, Block C long-term settlement, this week's rebar lot and concrete breaks, the slab-on-grade compaction results, the podium deflection check, the basement seepage assessment, and the reinforcement cover on foundation and exterior work — and let me know by 07/20/2026 which are cleared and which are not.

If any item cannot be verified in time, we would rather delay the pour than release non-conforming work. [P15] 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
[P16] Governing specification. Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025), governs. Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill. Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) expressly limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) requires, at every test location, dry density of not less than 95% of the D1557 Method C maximum dry density for the placed material and moisture content within −1% to +2% of the D1557 optimum. Article 3.4.D (p.5) makes the two criteria independent: density alone, or moisture alone, cannot establish acceptance. Article 3.7.B (p.5) requires each report to identify the D1557 denominators, measured dry density and moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation and an accept/reject disposition; Article 3.7.C (p.5) requires rework where the denominators used do not correspond to the material actually placed. Article 2.1.A/B/C (p.3) limits structural fill to well-graded granular material classified SM or SW-SM, with no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6, free of organic material, frozen soil, debris and particles greater than 3 in in largest dimension. Articles 1.5.A.1/A.2 and 2.1.D require source identification (gradation, Atterberg limits, USCS classification) and a D1557 Method C determination for each source and material change before placement. Article 1.6.A/B (p.3) prohibits fill over an unaccepted subgrade or on an untested preceding lift. Article 3.3.A (p.4) limits loose lifts to 12 in; Article 3.4.A (p.4) requires a witness test strip, hand-operated compaction in lifts not exceeding 6 in adjacent to walls, columns and utilities, and no heavy compaction equipment within 3 ft of walls before backfill balancing. Article 3.8.A (p.6) requires protection from precipitation, freezing and construction traffic and rework/retest of softened or disturbed areas. Articles 3.5 and 3.6 (p.5) address backfill against walls and completed-foundation settlement; their applicability to this fill is addressed below.
[P17] Acceptance limits produced. The D1557 Method C values on file are 128.4 pcf maximum dry density and 9.2% optimum moisture content (VMT-25-0918-P04, Result Summary, p.3; also carried on the Block A fill log, Cover B24 and Note 5). They are the only D1557 on file and are for the Larchwood Pit source. Applied as the provisional denominator they produce the limits in Table 1; the material-specific denominator for the Block A stockpile is not established (Finding 6).

[P19] What in the record establishes this basis for this fill. The governing basis is established by: (1) Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 1.3.E, 1.4.C, 2.1.A–D, 3.4.B/D and 3.7.B/C; (2) RFI 014 (response 06/23/2025), which confirms ASTM D1557 Method C for the engineered fill borrow; (3) Verification Register Item 012 (D1557 result on file, closed 09/22/2025) and Item 027 (both density and moisture criteria bind independently, closed 03/13/2026); (4) Geotechnical Report Rev.2 Section 9.5 (PDF p.20 / report p.19), which states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied; (5) the fill log Cover B25, which records Article 3.4.B as the acceptance basis, and Cover B24 / Note 5, which carry 128.4 pcf and 9.2%; and (6) the sealed D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025, which establishes those values for the Larchwood Pit source and states that the result supersedes any earlier Proctor result for Package A structural fill.
[P20] The record does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the D1557 determination for the stockpile north of Block C. The fill log identifies that stockpile as the borrow (Cover B23; Note 4); RFI 079 approved it “subject to gradation retest” (response 10/10/2025), and neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record. The only D1557 is for Larchwood Pit and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 4). The fill log’s Note 5 says the same Proctor was used on the Block B mass fill, but that is a Contractor assertion, not a stockpile determination. Pending that determination, 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is applied as the only D1557 on file, and the density results are provisional, not certified.
[P21] The D698/Wexford Ridge report does not establish the basis for this fill: ASTM D698 is excluded by Article 1.2.A.1, and its Wexford Ridge Phase 1 material (CL-ML, 68% passing the No. 200 sieve, PI 11) would not meet Article 2.1.B. Nothing in the record states that the Wexford Ridge material is the Block A stockpile, and nothing ties the two; the report is not a determination on the material placed and cannot supply a denominator.
[P22] Article 3.5 and Article 3.6 — applicability. Article 3.5 applies to backfill against basement or foundation walls. The fill log describes the work as slab-on-grade structural fill and does not record wall-adjacent placement, balanced lifts, or a wall-strength release. The pad finish grade El. 748.6 is at the basement wall top El. 748.5 (Detail 1/S-201; Sheet S-102), and A-501 General Note 6 requires backfill within 24 in of the wall to be granular, hand-placed and compacted per Section 31 20 00. Where any part of the pad abuts the basement wall, Article 3.5.A/B applies and the record must include the wall 28-day strength or permanent lateral support release and the balanced-lift record; neither is in the package. This is a scope and record condition on the wall interface; it is not a basis for accepting the fill. Article 3.6 is a completed-foundation-system tolerance (1.0 in total, 0.5 in differential over 30 ft). It is not a lift-acceptance criterion, no Block A settlement monitoring points are shown in the record, and Block C monitoring is under Item 051. Fill acceptance under 3.4.B is a prerequisite to the 3.6 evaluation; this record does not use 3.6 to accept the fill.
[P24] 4.  FINDINGS
[P25] Each finding cites the document and page it rests on. The recomputation of the four tests is set out in Table 1 at Finding 3.
[P26] Finding 1 — The governing acceptance standard is ASTM D1557 Method C, not ASTM D698. Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill; Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) sets the 95% density and −1%/+2% moisture criteria against that D1557 result. Verification Register Item 027 (closed 03/13/2026) confirms both criteria bind independently. Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), Section 9.5 (PDF p.20 / report p.19), states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. The Block A slab-on-grade fill is structural fill under Article 1.3.A, not common fill under Article 2.2.A, so Article 3.4.B applies. The Article 2.1.A/B/C material requirements that attach to that classification are addressed in Finding 6.
[P27] Finding 2 — SF-26-0708 is reported against the wrong standard and a borrow that is not tied to this fill, and it omits the moisture criterion. Report SF-26-0708 §3 (p.1) identifies ASTM D698 Method A, maximum dry density 118.6 pcf, optimum moisture 12.1%, Curve of Record VMT-2024-0403-P1B. That curve is the Wexford Ridge Phase 1 off-site borrow (VMT-2024-0403-P1B, p.1), a CL-ML silty clay with 68% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 11 (pp.1–2). That material would not meet Spec 31 20 00 Article 2.1.B (p.3), which limits structural fill to 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 6. The report does not state that the Wexford Ridge material is the stockpile north of Block C, and nothing in the record ties the two; what is clear is that D698 is not the acceptance method and the 118.6 pcf denominator is not the D1557 value for any Package A structural fill. The 103.6% to 106.3% compaction values in SF-26-0708 are computed against 118.6 pcf and are not valid against the 128.4 pcf D1557 value. The report also recites only the density requirement in §4 (p.1), has no moisture-deviation or moisture pass/fail column in §5 (pp.1–2), and accepts the fill “for density” in §6 (p.2). That is contrary to Spec 3.4.D (p.5) and the reporting requirements of 3.7.B (p.5). The only D1557 on file describes a well-graded silty sand and gravel, USCS SM/SW-SM, 9.4% passing the No. 200 sieve and non-plastic (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1); that material would meet Article 2.1.A/B for the Larchwood Pit sample, but the report is not a determination on the Block A stockpile.
[P28] Finding 3 — Against the only D1557 on file, density passes arithmetically at all four locations, but moisture fails at FD-14 and FD-17 and the density result is not certifiable for the placed stockpile. Table 1 recomputes each result against 128.4 pcf / 9.2%, the only D1557 on file. The correct percent compaction is dry density ÷ 128.4 × 100; the correct moisture deviation is measured moisture minus 9.2%. The density column is marked provisional because 128.4 pcf is the Larchwood Pit value, not a D1557 determination on the stockpile actually placed (Finding 6).

3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
Governing specification. Specification Section 31 20 00, Earth Moving, Rev.3 dated 03/06/2026 (supersedes Rev.2 of 11/14/2025), governs. Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill. Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) expressly limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) requires, at every test location, dry density of not less than 95% of the D1557 Method C maximum dry density for the placed material and moisture content within −1% to +2% of the D1557 optimum. Article 3.4.D (p.5) makes the two criteria independent: density alone, or moisture alone, cannot establish acceptance. Article 3.7.B (p.5) requires each report to identify the D1557 denominators, measured dry density and moisture, percent compaction, moisture deviation and an accept/reject disposition; Article 3.7.C (p.5) requires rework where the denominators used do not correspond to the material actually placed. Article 2.1.A/B/C (p.3) limits structural fill to well-graded granular material classified SM or SW-SM, with no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6, free of organic material, frozen soil, debris and particles larger than 3 in in their largest dimension. Articles 1.5.A.1/A.2 and 2.1.D require source identification (gradation, Atterberg limits, USCS classification) and a D1557 Method C determination for each source and material change before placement. Article 1.6.A/B (p.3) prohibits fill over an unaccepted subgrade or on an untested preceding lift. Article 3.3.A (p.4) limits loose lifts to 12 in; Article 3.4.A (p.4) requires a witness test strip, hand-operated compaction in lifts not exceeding 6 in adjacent to walls, columns and utilities, and no heavy compaction equipment within 3 ft of walls before backfill balancing. Article 3.8.A (p.6) requires protection from precipitation, freezing and construction traffic and rework/retest of softened or disturbed areas. Articles 3.5 and 3.6 (p.5) address backfill against walls and completed-foundation settlement; their applicability to this fill is addressed below.
Acceptance limits produced. The D1557 Method C values on file are 128.4 pcf maximum dry density and 9.2% optimum moisture content (VMT-25-0918-P04, Result Summary, p.3; also carried on the Block A fill log, Cover B24 and Note 5). They are the only D1557 on file and are for the Larchwood Pit source. Applied as the provisional denominator they produce the limits in Table 1; the material-specific denominator for the Block A stockpile is not established (Finding 6).

What in the record establishes this basis for this fill. The governing basis is established by: (1) Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 1.3.E, 1.4.C, 2.1.A–D, 3.4.B/D and 3.7.B/C; (2) RFI 014 (response 06/23/2025), which confirms ASTM D1557 Method C for the engineered fill borrow; (3) Verification Register Item 012 (D1557 result on file, closed 09/22/2025) and Item 027 (both density and moisture criteria bind independently, closed 03/13/2026); (4) Geotechnical Report Rev.2 Section 9.5 (PDF p.20 / report p.19), which states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied; (5) the fill log Cover B25, which records Article 3.4.B as the acceptance basis, and Cover B24 / Note 5, which carry 128.4 pcf and 9.2%; and (6) the sealed D1557 report VMT-25-0918-P04 dated 09/18/2025, which establishes those values for the Larchwood Pit source and states that the result supersedes any earlier Proctor result for Package A structural fill.
The record does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the D1557 determination for the stockpile north of Block C. The fill log identifies that stockpile as the borrow (Cover B23; Note 4); RFI 079 approved it “subject to gradation retest” (response 10/10/2025), and neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record. The only D1557 is for Larchwood Pit and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 4). The fill log’s Note 5 says the same Proctor was used on the Block B mass fill, but that is a Contractor assertion, not a stockpile determination. Pending that determination, 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is applied as the only D1557 on file, and the density results are provisional, not certified.
The D698/Wexford Ridge report does not establish the basis for this fill: ASTM D698 is excluded by Article 1.2.A.1, and its Wexford Ridge Phase 1 material (CL-ML, 68% passing the No. 200 sieve, PI 11) would not meet Article 2.1.B. Nothing in the record states that the Wexford Ridge material is the Block A stockpile, and nothing ties the two; the report is not a determination on the material placed and cannot supply a denominator.
Article 3.5 and Article 3.6 — applicability. Article 3.5 applies to backfill against basement or foundation walls. The fill log describes the work as slab-on-grade structural fill and does not record wall-adjacent placement, balanced lifts, or a wall-strength release. The pad finish grade El. 748.6 is at the basement wall top El. 748.5 (Detail 1/S-201), and A-501 General Note 6 requires backfill within 24 in of the wall to be granular, hand-placed and compacted per Section 31 20 00. Where any part of the pad abuts the basement wall, Article 3.5.A/B applies and the record must include the wall 28-day strength or permanent lateral support release and the balanced-lift record; neither is in the package. This is a scope and record condition on the wall interface; it is not a basis for accepting the fill. Article 3.6 is a completed-foundation-system tolerance (1.0 in total, 0.5 in differential over 30 ft). It is not a lift-acceptance criterion, no Block A settlement monitoring points are shown in the record, and Block C monitoring is under Item 051. Fill acceptance under 3.4.B is a prerequisite to the 3.6 evaluation; this record does not use 3.6 to accept the fill.

4.  FINDINGS
Each finding cites the document and page it rests on. The recomputation of the four tests is set out in Table 1 at Finding 3.
Finding 1 — The governing acceptance standard is ASTM D1557 Method C, not ASTM D698. Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 1.2.A.2 (p.1) makes ASTM D1557 the governing laboratory reference for Package A structural fill; Article 1.2.A.1 (p.1) limits ASTM D698 to historical borrow characterization and states that it is not the acceptance basis. Articles 1.3.E (p.2), 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 maximum dry density and optimum moisture content to be determined on the material actually placed at each test location and before placement. Article 3.4.B (p.4) sets the 95% density and −1%/+2% moisture criteria against that D1557 result. Verification Register Item 027 (closed 03/13/2026) confirms both criteria bind independently. Geotechnical Report Rev.2 (02/14/2025), Section 9.5 (PDF p.20 / report p.19), states the same 95% D1557 / −1% to +2% basis and requires both criteria to be satisfied. The Block A slab-on-grade fill is structural fill under Article 1.3.A, not common fill under Article 2.2.A, so Article 3.4.B applies. The Article 2.1.A/B/C material requirements that attach to that classification are addressed in Findings 6 and 6A.
Finding 2 — SF-26-0708 is reported against the wrong standard and a borrow that is not tied to this fill, and it omits the moisture criterion. Report SF-26-0708 §3 (p.1) identifies ASTM D698 Method A, maximum dry density 118.6 pcf, optimum moisture 12.1%, Curve of Record VMT-2024-0403-P1B. That curve is the Wexford Ridge Phase 1 off-site borrow (VMT-2024-0403-P1B, p.1), a CL-ML silty clay with 68% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 11 (pp.1–2). That material would not meet Spec 31 20 00 Article 2.1.B (p.3), which limits structural fill to 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and PI 6. The report does not state that the Wexford Ridge material is the stockpile north of Block C, and nothing in the record ties the two; what is clear is that D698 is not the acceptance method and the 118.6 pcf denominator is not the D1557 value for any Package A structural fill. The individual reported compaction values are 105.2% (FD-14), 104.1% (FD-15), 103.6% (FD-16) and 106.3% (FD-17), all computed against 118.6 pcf and not valid against the 128.4 pcf D1557 value. The report also recites only the density requirement in §4 (p.1), has no moisture-deviation or moisture pass/fail column in §5 (pp.1–2), and accepts the fill “for density” in §6 (p.2). That is contrary to Spec 3.4.D (p.5) and the reporting requirements of 3.7.B (p.5). The only D1557 on file describes a well-graded silty sand and gravel, USCS SM/SW-SM, 9.4% passing the No. 200 sieve and non-plastic (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1); that material would meet Article 2.1.A/B for the Larchwood Pit sample, but the report is not a determination on the Block A stockpile.
Finding 3 — Against the only D1557 on file, density passes arithmetically at all four locations, but moisture fails at FD-14 and FD-17 and the density result is not certifiable for the placed stockpile. Table 1 recomputes each result against 128.4 pcf / 9.2%, the only D1557 on file. The correct percent compaction is dry density ÷ 128.4 × 100; the correct moisture deviation is measured moisture minus 9.2%. The density column is marked provisional because 128.4 pcf is the Larchwood Pit value, not a D1557 determination on the stockpile actually placed (Finding 6).
Table 1 — Tests FD-14 through FD-17 recomputed against ASTM D1557 Method C (128.4 pcf, 9.2%). All four tests at El. 748.6, Lift 6. Inputs from SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; D1557 values from VMT-25-0918-P04 p.3.
[TABLE]
Test | Location | Dry density (pcf) | Moisture (%) | % comp. vs 128.4 | Density (provisional) | w dev. from 9.2% | Moisture 8.2–11.2% | Test disposition
FD-14 | Grid B-3 | 124.8 | 6.1 | 97.2 | PASS* | −3.1 | FAIL | NOT ACCEPTED — moisture
FD-15 | Grid D-5 | 123.5 | 9.8 | 96.2 | PASS* | +0.6 | PASS | NOT ACCEPTED — basis
FD-16 | Grid F-4 | 122.9 | 10.4 | 95.7 | PASS* | +1.2 | PASS | NOT ACCEPTED — basis

FD-14 is 6.1% moisture, 3.1 percentage points below optimum and 2.1 points below the 8.2% lower limit. FD-17 is 5.8%, 3.4 points below optimum and 2.4 points below the lower limit. FD-15 (9.8%) and FD-16 (10.4%) are within 8.2% to 11.2% and pass both numeric criteria. The density margin at FD-16 is thin: 122.9 pcf is 0.92 pcf (0.7 percentage point) above the 121.98 pcf minimum; a stockpile D1557 maximum dry density above about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. Under Spec 3.4.B and 3.4.D (pp.4–5), both criteria must be satisfied at each location; under 3.4.C.3 (p.5), failing results may not be averaged with passing results. Even if the two moisture failures were corrected, FD-15 and FD-16 could not be certified on a denominator that is not established for the placed material. Lift 6 therefore fails acceptance as tested.
* Provisional: 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the only D1557 on file (Larchwood Pit); it is not established as the D1557 for the stockpile north of Block C actually placed (Finding 6). The arithmetic pass is therefore not a certified density acceptance.
Finding 4 — The number and distribution of Lift 6 tests satisfy the frequency requirement, but the record covers only Lift 6. The pad area is 11,400 sf (Fill Log Cover B22; Notes 1; Daily Log row 24). At one test per 5,000 sf, 11,400/5,000 = 2.28, so three tests per lift are required; Article 3.7.A.1 also sets a floor of three tests per lift. Four tests were taken — FD-14 at Grid B-3, FD-15 at Grid D-5, FD-16 at Grid F-4 and FD-17 at Grid G-2 — all at El. 748.6 in Lift 6 (SF-26-0708 §5, pp.1–2; Fill Log Daily Log row 24). The frequency requirement is met with one test to spare. The log shows six lifts from El. 745.0 to El. 748.6, 3.6 ft total, at 8 in loose / 7.2 in compacted per lift (Cover B18–B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the 8 in Lift 6 thickness is within the 12 in limit. Lift 6 was placed in clear weather at 71–84 °F with no precipitation (Daily Log row 24), and no frozen material is recorded, consistent with Article 3.3.D. RFI 065 (response 09/22/2025, issued under Spec Rev.1) states one test per 500 sf. Article 3.4 was restructured in Rev.2 (11/14/2025) and Article 3.4.B was clarified in Rev.3 (03/06/2026), both later than the RFI; Rev.3’s 5,000 sf / minimum three per lift is the current contract text, and no ASI or change order adopting the 500 sf figure is in the record. I apply Rev.3. If RFI 065 were held to govern, 11,400 sf would require 23 tests per lift, not 4, and the frequency requirement would fail as well. The Contractor should obtain written confirmation that RFI 065 is superseded. The other five lifts are outside SF-26-0708 and are addressed in Finding 7.
Finding 5 — The testing was performed by the Owner’s independent laboratory, but the report and record do not establish all of the Article 1.4.B personnel, calibration and reporting requirements. The report is sealed by Talia Brennard, PE (p.2) and bears Vantree’s certification. The D1557 report states that the Laboratory is contracted to the Owner (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.4, Note 3), consistent with Spec 1.4.A. SF-26-0708 shows Vantree as the testing laboratory, Thornbury State University as client, a Troxler Model 3440 gauge (serial 34-047162), calibration dated 02/06/2026, standard counts of 2,478 density / 738 moisture, site standardization on 07/08/2026 before the first test, 60-second counts and ASTM D6938 direct transmission (p.1). Those entries describe the gauge and the daily standardization, but they do not establish the whole of Article 1.4.B: (a) the calibration certificate is only “on file” and was not provided; (b) there is no record of the operator’s current radiation-safety training or documented competence in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures, as 1.4.B requires; (c) the probe depth is 6 in while the compacted lift is 7.2 in (Fill Log Cover B21; Daily Log rows 19–24), so the bottom 1.2 in of the lift was not sampled and full-thickness compliance under 3.3.C is not demonstrated; (d) the report was issued on 07/09/2026 but records no issue time — the field work ended at 11:30 on 07/08, so any issue after 11:30 on 07/09 would exceed the 24-hour requirement of 3.7.B, and compliance is not demonstrated on the face of the report; and (e) as found in Finding 2, it reports density only and against the wrong D698 reference. The Article 1.4.B requirements are therefore partially described but not verified; the calibration certificate and personnel records must be produced before the testing record can be relied on (Action 8).
Finding 6 — The D1557 denominator and the Article 2.1.A/B/C material requirements are not established for the stockpile actually placed, and the FD-16 density margin is too thin to absorb a different Proctor. The fill log identifies the borrow as the stockpile north of Block C, approved for reuse under RFI 079 (Fill Log Cover B23; Notes 4). It carries VMT-25-0918-P04, the Larchwood Pit D1557, as the governing Proctor (Cover B24; Notes 5). The only D1557 report in the record is for Larchwood Pit (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1) and expressly “pertains only to the sample tested” (p.4, Note 4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor letter TPM-25-079 is in the record, and there is no D1557 on the stockpile material. Spec 1.4.C (p.2) and 2.1.D (p.3) require the D1557 values to be those of the material actually placed, and 1.4.C requires a new D1557 where the placed material differs materially. The record therefore does not establish that 128.4 pcf / 9.2% is the correct denominator for the stockpile. That matters: FD-16 passes by only 0.92 pcf (0.7 percentage point), so a material-specific maximum dry density higher than about 129.4 pcf would make FD-16 fail the density criterion. The D1557 values used in Finding 3 are the correct method and the only D1557 on file, but they are not a substitute for the stockpile-specific determination.
Finding 6A — The same gap defeats Article 2.1.A/B/C compliance for the stockpile. Article 2.1.A (p.3) requires well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM D1557 Method C before placement. Article 2.1.B (p.3) requires no more than 12% passing the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6. Article 2.1.C (p.3) requires the fill to be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and particles larger than 3 in (largest dimension). Article 1.5.A.1 requires source identification including gradation, Atterberg limits and USCS classification before placement. The only material characterization in the record is for the Larchwood Pit D1557 sample: well-graded silty sand and gravel, USCS SM/SW-SM, 9.4% passing the No. 200 sieve, non-plastic (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.1). That would satisfy 2.1.A/B for that sample, but it is not the stockpile. The fill log identifies the stockpile north of Block C but records no gradation, Atterberg limits, USCS classification, or deleterious-material inspection for it (Cover B23; Notes 4). RFI 079 approved the stockpile “subject to gradation retest” and refers to letter TPM-25-079 (RFI Log row RFI 079, 10/10/2025); neither the retest nor the letter is in the record. Submittal 31-BR-A Rev.1 (borrow source qualification) was released with note markings on 07/17/2025 with the comment “Modified Proctor scheduled with Vantree,” and 31-PR-A (modified Proctor report) was accepted 09/22/2025 (Submittal Register rows 31-BR-A and 31-PR-A); neither identifies the Block A stockpile. The record therefore does not establish 2.1.A/B/C compliance for the material actually placed. This is an independent ground for rejection: even a moisture-compliant retest cannot be accepted until the stockpile is classified and tested, and the 3-in particle limit and the absence of organic material, frozen soil and debris must be verified by inspection and gradation.
Finding 7 — The record does not demonstrate that Lifts 1 through 5 were accepted, or that the subgrade and test-strip hold points were closed with test evidence. The fill log states that Lifts 1 through 5 are covered by FDR-BA-01 through FDR-BA-05, three tests per lift (Cover B31; Notes 6), and that each lift was tested before the next was placed (Notes 6; Daily Log rows 19–23). Those five reports are not in the review record, so their density/moisture results and dispositions cannot be checked. The log also records a rework of about 1,500 sf near Grid E-4 in Lift 5 for moisture correction (Daily Log row 23); no retest result for that rework is in the record. Daily Field Report No. 143 (06/30/2026) records 0.35 in of rain overnight after the Lift 5 shift; Daily Field Report No. 144 (07/01/2026) records 0.42 in overnight into 07/01. The two reports describe the same overnight period with different readings; the higher 0.42 in value is used here. No placement occurred from 07/01 to 07/07 (Daily Log row 24), so the Lift 5 surface was exposed to that water before Lift 6. The package contains no Lift 5 protection or post-rain retest record for that surface. The subgrade proof-roll is recorded only as a log statement — loaded tandem-axle dump truck, Vantree present, 06/18/2026 — with written acceptance said to be memo TPM-26-063 dated 06/18/2026 (Cover B26; Notes 2); the log does not record the 20-ton loaded tandem required by RFI 118 (response 03/09/2026), and the memo is not attached. The test strip is recorded as executed 06/19/2026, witnessed by Vantree and Thelbridge, with six passes (Cover B27; Notes 3), but no test-strip results demonstrating Article 3.4.B compliance are in the record. For Lift 6 itself, the log records six smooth-drum passes and four pneumatic/plate passes (Daily Log row 24), matching the six-pass test-strip pattern; the procedure appears to have been followed, but procedure alone does not cure the moisture failures. The log records the Wacker plate at edges and tie-ins but not the loose thickness of those hand-compacted lifts; nor does it identify the walls or edges where the 3-ft heavy-equipment setback of Article 3.4.A applies, or record compliance with it. Spec 1.6.A/B (p.3) and 3.4.A/C (pp.4–5) make these hold points and prior-lift acceptances prerequisites. They must be produced before the fill as a whole can be accepted, even if Lift 6 is later reworked and retested.
Finding 8 — The open moisture RFI does not change the criteria. RFI 125, raised 07/08/2026, asks for an interpretation of the moisture criteria on SF-26-0708; the RFI log shows no response and status Open (RFI Log row RFI 125). No waiver, variance or revision to Spec 31 20 00 is in the record. The criteria of Article 3.4.B apply as written. If the Contractor disputes the nuclear moisture values, ASTM D2216 is the referee method under Article 1.2.A.4; a referee result would still be evaluated against the same 8.2% to 11.2% window. RFI 065’s earlier “one test per 500 sf” response is not a basis to alter the later Rev.3 frequency for the reasons in Finding 4; Rev.3 governs, subject to the written confirmation recommended there.
Finding 9 — The Contractor’s 07/14/2026 pour-readiness statement is a density-only claim against the wrong reference; it is not acceptance evidence. The notification states that “all four tests exceed 95% requirement” (S. Kendrow email, 07/14/2026, item (b)). That statement refers only to density and is computed against the wrong D698 reference; it does not address the moisture failures at FD-14 and FD-17. It is a Contractor assertion, not test evidence, and cannot support acceptance.
Finding 10 — The D1557 report’s stated curve fit does not exactly reproduce 128.4 pcf at 9.2%; the difference is immaterial to this determination. The sealed report reports 128.4 pcf at 9.2% and states that its curve fit is a second-order polynomial through the five primary points with the peak located by first-derivative solution (VMT-25-0918-P04, p.3). A least-squares quadratic through those five points (6.2%/124.8 pcf, 7.5%/127.1 pcf, 9.2%/128.4 pcf, 10.8%/126.7 pcf, 12.4%/123.5 pcf) peaks at about 128.20 pcf at 9.04%, so 95% of the fitted peak would be 121.79 pcf and the corresponding moisture window would be 8.04% to 11.04%. FD-16 at 122.9 pcf and 10.4% still passes either basis; FD-14 and FD-17 still fail moisture;

steps.message:
All required deliverables exist at the exact paths, are complete, and pass the format, content, register and hard-limit checks.

## Deliverable

**`/filesystem/Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Fill_Compaction_2026-0708.docx`** — 10-page Materials Acceptance Record built on `Thelbridge_Materials_Acceptance_Record_TEMPLATE.docx`, dated 07/16/2026, signed by Karen Tarbray. All five template sections are present in order, with four tables and no placeholders.

## Determination: REJECTED

**Register entry:** Item 054 — **Status Closed; disposition REJECTED; verification date 07/16/2026.** The fill remains unaccepted. A new register item is required for the Lift 6 rework/retest and stockpile qualification.

## Basis and limits

- **Basis:** Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3 (03/06/2026), Articles 1.2.A.1/A.2, 1.3.E, 1.4.C, 2.1.A–D, 3.4.B/D and 3.7.B/C — ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed. ASTM D698 is expressly not the acceptance basis.
- **Density:** ≥95% of 128.4 pcf = **121.98 pcf** (report rounds to 122.0 pcf).
- **Moisture:** **8.2%–11.2%** (9.2% optimum −1%/+2%).
- **Material:** USCS SM/SW-SM; ≤12% passing No. 200; PI ≤6; no organic material, frozen soil, debris or particles >3 in.
- **Procedural limits:** D1557 per source; subgrade proof-roll and prior-lift hold points; witnessed test strip; 8 in loose/7.2 in compacted within 12 in; hand lifts ≤6 in and 3-ft setback; wall backfill under Article 3.5; protection under 3.8.A; settlement under 3.6; capillary break under 2.3.

The 128.4 pcf/9.2% D1557 is the only one on file and is for **Larchwood Pit**, not the stockpile north of Block C actually placed. The RFI 079 gradation retest and letter TPM-25-079 are missing, and the Larchwood Pit report “pertains only to the sample tested.” The density results are therefore provisional, not certified. The Article 2.1.A/B/C material requirements are likewise not established for the stockpile.

## Results

| Test | Dry density (pcf) | Moisture (%) | % comp. vs 128.4 | Outcome |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| FD-14 | 124.8 | 6.1 | 97.2 | **Moisture fail** — 2.1 points below 8.2% |
| FD-15 | 123.5 | 9.8 | 96.2 | Numeric pass; not accepted on basis |
| FD-16 | 122.9 | 10.4 | 95.7 | Numeric pass; only 0.92 pcf margin; not accepted on basis |
| FD-17 | 126.1 | 5.8 | 98.2 | **Moisture fail** — 2.4 points below 8.2% |
